It has been revealed that ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said that crypto needs some of the features that made housing a safe investment for earlier generations. "We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets," Buterin wrote in a post on X on Nov. 18.

Industry observers note that the post came a day after economist Peter Tulip published his own post on housing in Raleigh, North Carolina. According to Tulip, looser zoning rules in the city set off a construction boom and pushed real rents down 15% between 2022 and 2025.

In his post, Buterin first pointed to a benefit of young people putting their savings into stocks and crypto instead of real estate.

"One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities," he wrote.

According to recent reports, still, the Ethereum co-founder noted that housing has had one advantage over stocks and crypto. He described it as "a culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can't easily liquidate.".

"Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior," Buterin added.

Ether was trading at $1,808 on Wednesday.

Buterin has written about housing and urban planning before. He has supported the YIMBY movement for denser development in cities for several years.

It has been revealed that in 2022, Buterin argued for a land value tax. According to him, such a tax would lower the upfront cost of buying a home and discourage speculation on vacant lots.

It has been revealed that in 2025, the Ethereum co-founder called the housing market a "confusing market of peculiar NFTs." According to Buterin, what is really being sold under the label of square footage is the right to live in a particular city. At the time, he also mentioned that legalizing dense development speeds up the economy and benefits even people who prefer single-family homes.

  • Investors in the upcoming round valued the company at $3.5 billion, a person familiar with the deal told TechCrunch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Science Corporation, the medical technology startup founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak in 2021, raised a $400 million Series D, the firm stated in a blog post.

Investors in the upcoming round valued the company at $3.5 billion, a person familiar with the deal told TechCrunch. Those backers included Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator, and PLC Neurotech.

Hodak, who talked his way into a graduate neuroscience lab as a college student and has pursued biotechnology ever since, co-founded Science to leverage new technologies to understand and interact with the brain.

Recent findings suggest that science’s first product is PRIMA, a wearable and implantable chip that helps people with age-related macular degeneration recover some vision. The device is approved in Europe and available in Germany, as well as being trialed for fresh conditions.

Hodak declared that the device is now being trialed for patients with another blindness-causing condition, Stargardt disease, while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.

Sources indicate that with the funding, the tech giant aims to bring the device to the United States through the FDA’s Humanitarian Device Exemption, which lets experimental medical technology be used to treat rare conditions. Science has convinced the FDA that advanced macular degeneration in both eyes is uncommon enough to let them seek approval to use the device on people in the U.S.

Still, the startup’s big ambition and founding purpose is connecting directly to the human brain through a bio-hybrid sensor built from a combination of cultured neurons and silicon. The firm is currently designing initial human trials of the device with Yale neurosurgery professor Murat Günel, who told TechCrunch it could offer potential treatments for Parkinson’s disease, among other brain injuries and illnesses.

MEXC confirmed that its Global Card service will be discontinued on November 18, according to the exchange's announcement. The firm cites service adjustments by its third-party card issuer. From the deadline, existing cards can no longer be used for transactions, and latest card applications are suspended.

Customers have two things to take care of before the service ends.

First, the remaining card balance has to be withdrawn: the Withdraw button on the Global Card page sends the funds to the Fiat account.

Second, subscriptions linked to the card should be cancelled or switched to another payment method. Unfortunately for cardholders, recurring payments will most likely fail if they stay on the old card.

Industry observers note that if there's still a balance when the service ends, MEXC will credit it to the Spot account, so owners will simply receive their funds back. It's important to keep in mind that pending card transactions need time to settle, which is why the balance snapshot comes on November 21, three days after the shutdown. The amount will be credited within three business days of the snapshot. Users do not need to take any action.

Recent findings suggest that refunds for previous card transactions will be credited to the Fiat account once MEXC receives them. Pending cashback will be credited automatically as scheduled. Elite VVIP users with zero-fee benefits will be refunded too, though the eligible fees return to their Spot accounts only before December 15.

Transaction history, card orders and cashback records stay available on the Global Card page for three months after the service ends, so it's worth saving anything needed before access ends.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain types of services to third parties all the time, so witnessing a similar situation is more than a possibility here. Realistically, the shutdown is somewhat inconvenient rather than dangerous, as the balances are returned automatically. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

Breaking: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a upcoming startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
  • According to recent reports, on Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding.
  • The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a upcoming startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.

According to recent reports, on Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The tech giant’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a proposal that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.

The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage. Pedestal states the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.

In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the tech giant reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further.

CEO Raj Aggarwal claims contemporary AI systems are particularly useful for dealing with that data. “The challenge is that the data is messy and it’s constantly changing,” Aggarwal told TechCrunch. “It’s disparate because it sits in so many legacy systems. That’s what makes it hard.”.

It has been revealed that supply chain AI has become a particularly hot space in recent months as alumni from autonomous driving teams look to launch their own startups. The supply chain startup Atomic, launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory. Another venture called Loop was launched by Uber alums to focus on predictive analytics.

Sources indicate that as Aggarwal sees it, deliveries are particularly well-suited to training reinforcement learning systems. Because of their high volumes and easily measured outcomes, it’s easy to fine-tune contemporary AI systems toward what’s working and away from what isn’t.

Perhaps most importantly, it’s the kind of problem that can have an immediate effect on a client’s bottom line, making it easy to justify the expense.

“If you can get it right,” he told TechCrunch, “you can have really significant impact.”.

Cardano-based stablecoin DJED has announced its sunset, as DJED and SHEN services will wind down on December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC.

DJED represents a crypto-backed, overcollateralized stablecoin protocol on Cardano whose US-dollar peg is maintained algorithmically against an ADA reserve (with SHEN as the reserve coin), rather than by fiat reserves.

"DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC," a DJED-focused X account wrote.

ATTN: DJED & SHEN Holders DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Please redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN you hold before then. All redemptions are subject to the reserve ratio.

People are urged to redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN they hold before this deadline. Users are to redeem on the protocol and convert their DJED and SHEN back to ADA on the official Djed page. Users who hold DJED or SHEN in liquidity pools, lending markets, or other DeFi platforms are urged to withdraw those positions first, then redeem or swap.

Sources indicate that the Djed team stated all systems are fully operational and redemptions are now open, subject to the reserve ratio. It further added that the Djed protocol will be maintained and remain available until December 31, 2026. After this date, all remaining funds will be allocated to the outstanding DJED/SHEN holders once the wind-down is complete.

In a recent development, djed’s shutdown comes almost three years after its launch, which came in 2023. The stablecoin was officially rolled out on the Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023, and was developed by COTI in collaboration with the Cardano ecosystem to be used on DeFi protocols on Cardano as a stable alternative to volatile cryptocurrencies.

In positive news for the Cardano ecosystem, Monument Bank Limited has introduced tokenized deposits on the Midnight network, marking a milestone for the network and the decentralized finance ecosystem.

At present, Monument is the first UK bank to tokenize retail deposits on a public blockchain, offering clients a 5.2% AER fixed-term return on savings directly through its existing banking app, delivering institutional onchain finance through a familiar and user-friendly banking experience.

Up to £250 million of client deposits will be represented on Midnight in this opening phase, with deposits recorded one-to-one in sterling.

Latest Update: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January.
  • It has been revealed that the company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it stated, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year.
  • But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both newly introduced investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

It has been revealed that the company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it stated, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it indicates how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

According to recent reports, nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.”  Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic and OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a big financier of the data center build-out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

The company made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earnings call, Kress said Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”.

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the manufacturer will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

Huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with newly introduced investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

In a recent development, “We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress said on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that strive CEO Matt Cole has observed an interesting historical parallel between Bitcoin’s current price action and its performance ahead of SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin’s latest price decline may be setting the stage for a familiar market pattern, and history could give bulls reason to be optimistic. The benchmark cryptocurrency has suffered a sharp drop ahead of Anthropic’s upcoming red-hot stock market debut, echoing its 19% plunge in the 50 days leading up to SpaceX’s IPO earlier this year. However, if the historical pattern repeats, Bitcoin could be gearing up for a significant recovery, with a potential rebound toward $90,000 by February now drawing attention.

Industry observers note that strive CEO Matt Cole has observed an interesting historical parallel between Bitcoin’s current price action and its performance ahead of SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO. In the 50 days leading up to SpaceX’s $75 billion public debut on June 12, Bitcoin plunged 19%.

Now, with Anthropic preparing for a potential $64.4 billion IPO next week, BTC has posted a remarkably similar 18% decline over the same period, Cole noted in a post on X.

Sources indicate that at press time, Bitcoin was trading at $64,665, according to CoinGecko, extending its recent losses after breaking below the $70,000 mark on November 13. The cryptocurrency continued its downward slide over the weekend, falling beneath $67,000 as bearish pressure intensified.

The Strive chief noted that overlaying the two price movements reveals an almost identical pattern, raising the possibility that Bitcoin could be repeating its pre-SpaceX sell-off ahead of another historic market debut.

Bitcoin extended its decline after SpaceX’s market debut, reaching its lowest point 18 days later before reversing course. The subsequent rally lifted BTC 28% above its IPO-day closing price within 100 days.

“If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse rapidly over the next couple of months,” Cole opined.

If history repeats itself, Bitcoin could climb toward $90,000 by late February, Cole suggested.

Binance co-founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao also weighed in on the chart comparison, sharing the analysis on X and describing Cole’s findings as “interesting.”.

Sources indicate that however, the historical comparison comes with crucial caveats. Bitcoin’s sell-off ahead of the SpaceX IPO unfolded alongside market concerns over potential BTC sales by Michael Saylor’s Strategy, suggesting that factors beyond the anticipated listing may have contributed to the decline. As a result, attributing the entire downturn to IPO-related sentiment would overlook other pressures weighing on the market at the time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a week after Binance suffered the biggest cyberattack seen in the history of the crypto market, the onchain monitoring platform Whale Alert has spotted the hacker moving some of the funds in large quantities.

The transfer has raised concerns across the crypto community about what the hacker might be up to and about the possibility of Binance recovering the stolen funds, especially after they are moved to another wallet.

Although the source did not provide sufficient details about the highly concerning transfer, it highlighted that the attacker behind the 2026 Binance hack moved 60,000 ETH on Wednesday in 2026.

In a recent development, the broader crypto market has continued to suffer extreme volatility since the attack happened in late October. Hence, the total portion of Ethereum tokens transferred from the stolen stash is now worth $108.78 million at ETH’s current market price.

While the reason behind the sudden move after a few weeks of silence remains uncertain, further data demonstrated that the assets were moved in five separate transfers of 12,000 ETH each.

Notably, each transaction was worth between $21.75 million and $21.77 million, and they were identified as Binance’s stolen funds because they were all moved from a wallet labeled 'Binance hack' in 2026.

Considering the history of the transferred funds, the move has sparked speculation that the hacker might already be preparing to spend the stolen funds, further sabotaging Binance’s chances of full recovery.

However, it is vital to note that there is no evidence that the attacker has sold the Ethereum, as the receiving wallet has not been identified.

Breaking: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed US robotics companies the data they need

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S.
  • In a recent development, the funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading.
  • In a recent development, companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks, but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S. AI and robotics companies build models that can operate in physical environments.

In a recent development, the funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading. It also includes $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

In a recent development, companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks, but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult. Startups, including Mecka AI, XDOF, and MicroAGI, are already tackling the problem by collecting real-world data for robotics training. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs aims to compete with them.

In a recent development, humyn Labs has developed its own two-camera hardware to record people performing everyday tasks. It then uses its software to process and label the footage, which means tagging what happens in each clip so AI can learn from it. The startup collects data across over 20 countries in Latin America and Asia, with Brazil, India, and South Korea serving as its main hubs, co-founder Manish Agarwal (pictured above, right) said in an interview.

In a recent development, agarwal, the former CEO of Indian gaming company Nazara Technologies, founded Humyn Labs in February with Ishank Gupta (pictured above, left), a former executive at the brewing giant AB InBev. The duo previously founded Kratos Studios, now known as KGeN. KGeN has a network of contributors across emerging markets, and that network helps Humyn Labs collect data in people’s homes, the founders told TechCrunch.

It has been revealed that collecting footage of human activity is only part of the challenge, Agarwal said. He added that Humyn Labs also uses software to track hand movements, interactions with objects, and other details, turning raw recordings into data that AI models can learn from.

“Scale, diversity, and quality are important aspects, and they need to work in tandem,” Agarwal said.

Humyn Labs claims it has 12 paying customers, including frontier AI labs, robotics companies, and developers of world models. About 90% of its revenue comes from the U.S., Gupta said, though he declined to name specific customers.

The startup generated $10 million in revenue between April and October and has another $20 million in signed contracts, Agarwal told TechCrunch, adding that a further $20 million in deals has yet to be finalized.

That growth has also increased Humyn Labs’ need for working capital, Agarwal stated, explaining the $21 million venture debt component. The startup pays workers and data collection partners daily or weekly but typically waits 30 to 60 days to receive payments from its AI lab customers. Borrowing helps bridge that gap and is less dilutive than selling more equity, he said.

Over the last few months, India has emerged as a hub for collecting training data for so-called physical AI, with startups, including Human Archive and BuildAI, tapping into the country’s large workforce to record people performing everyday tasks. However, the practice has also raised questions about privacy and consent, particularly when people are recorded inside their homes.

According to recent reports, agarwal mentioned Humyn Labs collects data from people doing their usual work or household chores instead of asking them to perform staged activities. The startup works with local partners to identify collection sites and oversee the process. “The worker is a worker who is incentivized, but he needs to be monitored and supervised for the right input,” he stated.

Humyn Labs presently has 51 full-time employees, most based in Bengaluru, plus a network of local partners across the countries where it collects data, Agarwal noted.

Back is the cryptographer behind Hashcash. The algorithm laid the groundwork for proof-of-work, and Satoshi Nakamoto cited it in the Bitcoin white paper. Back was also one of the first people Satoshi contacted before the launch of Bitcoin in 2009.

Industry observers note that the Blockstream CEO has posted about the 200WMA on X several times this year. On March 27, he wrote that the "200wma passes $59k." The indicator was just above $60,000 in early May, and on May 30, Back reported that it had crossed $61,000. In September, the 200WMA rose above $65,000 for the first time.

Sources indicate that in a follow-up post in May, Back cited a maxim of the late Charlie Munger. According to Munger, an investor who buys only high-quality assets when they trade at the 200-week moving average would beat the S&P 500 over time. Back also noted that Munger and Warren Buffett never embraced Bitcoin.

Industry observers note that in mid-September, Bitcoin was trading at around $76,000 to $77,000. At that time, the gap between the price and the 200WMA was more than $10,000.

According to recent reports, on Wednesday, Bitcoin was trading at $64,150, about 6% below the 200WMA. On Nov. 15, BTC dropped as low as $62,000 before bouncing 5.5%. Back called the move "bouncy" in a post on X.

Sources indicate that in a CNBC interview on Nov. 12, Back said that Bitcoin could reach $1 million by 2028. According to Back, more than 95% of potential institutional inflows into Bitcoin are still ahead. He named investment trusts, asset managers and corporate treasuries among the buyers, and he said that their buying was just beginning.

Back also pointed to the Bitcoin halving in the spring of 2028. He said that miners would sell fewer coins after it.

He made a similar point at Paris Blockchain Week in April. "When the Bitcoin price is low, the miners have to sell a bigger proportion… and when the price is higher, they don't have to sell as much," Back stated at the time.

AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Felicis leads $7.5M bet on Unsiloed AI to make enterprise documents usable by AI agents

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (902 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge.
  • Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures.
  • According to recent reports, business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge. Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to tackle that problem, aiming to help enterprises make their documents more accessible to AI agents through specialized technology.

Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures. Angel investors Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner also participated.

According to recent reports, business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately. But getting the information wrong can lead to costly mistakes for businesses, and the impact could be severe in the case of a bank, hospital, or a law firm, as they rely on these documents for their daily work.

Sources indicate that unsiloed aims to solve this problem with software that breaks down complex documents, extracts information from tables, charts, and other elements, and turns it into structured data that AI agents can use. The technology also demonstrates where the extracted information came from in the original document, so businesses can check the results rather than take the AI’s output at face value.

“The problem with LLMs is they’re inherently probabilistic,” noted Unsiloed co-founder and CEO Aman Mishra (pictured above, right) in an interview. “There is going to be some deviation induced. There is going to be some hallucination involved, and that has a massive negative impact downstream.”.

It has been revealed that mishra co-founded Unsiloed with Adnan Abbas (pictured above, left), his former classmate at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. The two joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch after spending some time developing the technology.

According to recent reports, unsiloed is already working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, Mishra told TechCrunch. One bank is using its technology to process documents, while a law firm has deployed it on its own servers to handle contracts and old case files, he noted, without naming either customer. Mishra, however, named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, saying it uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents.

Recent findings suggest that the San Francisco-headquartered startup has entered a market that is already crowded and includes specialized document-processing startups such as Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon. Businesses also sometimes use general-purpose AI models to extract information from documents, giving Unsiloed another set of competitors.

Mishra told TechCrunch that Unsiloed’s advantage lies in how it processes complex documents. The startup uses what it calls “dual-stream” vision models, which handle text and image data separately, along with a technique called “heat map-based chunking” that helps identify the most vital parts of a document.

According to recent reports, “In one of the streams you have the text tokens, in the other stream you have the exact image tokens,” Mishra said. “This is something that we have spent a lot of time architecting.”.

Recent findings suggest that the technology then directs more computing power toward areas such as figures, numbers, and charts. Unsiloed also uses a specialized decoder that takes industry-specific terminology into account, helping it distinguish between terms that can mean different things in different business contexts.

Supporting those claims, Mishra pointed to a test involving 542 financial documents supplied by an enterprise customer. Unsiloed achieved 99.78% accuracy across roughly 84,000 extracted data points, per a technical brief shared by the startup. The test compared Unsiloed with major AI models, Microsoft’s Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer’s in-house extraction tool. The results have, however, not been independently verified.

Unsiloed also claims to have outperformed competing AI document-processing tools on olmOCR-Bench, a public benchmark developed by Allen AI. In tests conducted by the startup, Unsiloed scored 88.0, compared with 66.0 for Reducto’s agentic system and 39.9 for Unstructured. The benchmark covered 1,403 PDF pages and tested how well the systems handled tables, mathematical expressions, scanned documents, and complex layouts.

Unsiloed’s pricing, Mishra mentioned, starts at one cent per page. He asserted that the startup’s approach also helps keep its costs down by directing computing power toward the parts of a document that need the most attention, instead of processing every section in the same way.

It has been revealed that currently, Unsiloed has a headcount of seven people. The startup, Mishra said, aims to use the fresh funding to hire more researchers and engineers, expand its sales efforts, and develop proprietary datasets to improve its technology.

The Single Asset Vault amendment on the XRP Ledger is getting closer to activation on the mainnet as validator support builds for the network’s preparation to enable better DeFi functionality.

Recent findings suggest that according to data from XRPScan, the SingleAssetVault amendment, or XLS-65, has received yes votes from 25 of 35 trusted validators, at the moment standing at 71.43% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of 35 votes (29) to start its 14-day countdown to activation. That means it needs four more votes to get there and could reach the magic number before the end of 2026.

The XRP Ledger’s amendment process requires a proposed amendment to be approved by more than 80% of trusted validators for 14 days before it is implemented. Validator support may shift during this time, and if the required 80% threshold is lost, activation may be delayed.

The Single Asset Vault amendment creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. The amendment introduces a Vault object that defines the state of a tokenized vault, and the Vault entry is one of the ledger entry types it provides.

Recent findings suggest that the Vault object holds important information such as available assets, shares, total value, and other relevant information. Customers can create a Vault object with the VaultCreate transaction; the Vault object is tracked in an Owner Directory owned by the Vault Owner account.

The XRP Ledger lending amendment has gained additional yes votes. According to XRPScan, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, also known as XLS-66, has received 24 yes votes out of 35 trusted validators, meaning it has 68.57% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of the 35 votes (29) to trigger a 14-day activation countdown.

This implies that there are five votes left for it to reach this threshold, with the possibility of it securing the required number of votes before the end of 2026 as well.

According to XRP enthusiasts, LendingProtocolV1_1 represents the biggest amendment for unlocking capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger and is anticipated by institutional and retail owners.

Recent findings suggest that my passport book is nearly out of blank pages, and I’m starting to worry that my next trip will require an emergency upgrade to make it through customs. But as a frequent flyer and style writer, one thing I don’t stress over is what to wear to the airport. Between maxing out my PTO and logging plenty of miles for work (including tons of in-transit testing for WH Travel Awards), I’ve mastered the art of the airport fit. And while I firmly believe that wearing jeans on a plane should land you on the no-fly list, I’m all about wearing something comfortable without looking like I’m wearing pajamas at the terminal.

In a recent development, that’s where the right pair of travel pants comes in clutch, hitting that happy medium between polished and comfortable. I’m talking about pants you can sit in for hours, sprint through a terminal in, and still wear straight to dinner without a second thought. Over time (and many, many flights), I’ve narrowed down the pairs that truly deliver: versatile, low-maintenance styles that work just as well in your suitcase as they do on your body, from takeoff to touchdown.

Industry observers note that the Vuori Halo Essential Wideleg pant has been at the top of my drawer since I got my first pair nearly a year ago. I’m obsessed with the super-soft and smooth polyester and elastane blend. It feels nearly pajama-like while looking way more polished than your average sweatpant (especially if you opt for a darker color like black or navy).

I often reach for this pant when getting dressed for the airport because I know I’ll be comfortable on the plane and that I’ll wear it at least once during my trip. The wide-leg silhouette skims the body in a really flattering way without looking baggy or oversized. It looks great paired with Vuori’s matching zip-up and my fave Dr. Scholl’s Time Off Sneaker for long-haul flights, but it just as easily dresses up with a cute sandal and a form-fitting tank or tee.

Oh, and the pant never wrinkles. It feels soft and cotton-like but since it's made from a buttery synthetic blend, it always looks sleek—more quiet luxury than airport chaos. The material isn’t too thick either, so I don’t find myself overheating while wearing it, even when I land in a sunny destination. I wore this pant while traveling to Mexico recently and felt totally comfortable from takeoff in Upcoming York until I arrived at the hotel.

If you’re looking for an under-$50 find that holds its own against pricier pairs, the Old Navy Linen-Blend Ankle Pant is it. Made from a 55% linen blend, it delivers the airy look and feel you want from linen—without the steep price tag most comparable styles carry.

It has been revealed that comfort-wise, it’s exactly what I want for a travel day: lightweight, breathable, and stylish. The secret is in the fabric. This pant blends linen with rayon, a semi-synthetic fiber derived from natural sources like wood pulp that’s known for being soft, smooth, and less prone to creasing than 100% linen. The result is breezy but cozy fabric that doesn’t feel remotely scratchy or itchy. I also love the clean, straight-leg silhouette and high waist that makes me feel put-together with next to zero effort.

I will say, this is one of those pairs I prefer to wear on the plane rather than pack, since it picks up a few more wrinkles when folded in a suitcase (it is still linen, after all). But once I put it on, the fabric bounces back nicely—and I end up reaching for it constantly throughout my trip. The pant is endlessly versatile: I’ll throw it on with flat sandals and a white tee for daytime exploring, then swap in a blouse and heels for dinner without missing a beat.

Industry observers note that if you didn’t know better, you might mistake the lululemon Daydrift High-Rise Wide-Leg Trouser for a lounge pant—but one mirror check and it’s giving Succession-coded energy. It’s my go-to for when I need to land and immediately be “on,” whether that’s heading to a meeting or traveling with colleagues.

According to recent reports, made primarily from nylon and elastane, this pant is breathable, sweat-wicking, and cool to the touch—exactly what I want for a long day on the go. It has a smooth, tailored look that resists wrinkling, making it especially suitcase-friendly. It also features a stretch waistband with an internal drawstring, which makes a significant difference when I’m sitting for hours or dealing with the general unpredictability of travel days.

I’ll wear it with my go-to Uniqlo Crew Neck T-Shirt and sneakers for a more casual, on-the-move look, but it just as easily leans corporate with a button-down or blazer. Swap in a silky top and heels and it even holds its own for evening looks. It’s that comfort and versatility that make it such a staple in my everyday and travel wardrobe.

It has been revealed that if you want something that feels barely there for a warm-weather vacation, the FP Movement Champ Is Here Pant is my top rec. Made from 100% nylon, it’s airy and flowy and allows for total free range of movement—perfect for long travel days or more active itineraries. And thanks to the barrel-leg silhouette (meaning it’s a bit wider at the knee area) and the subtle contrast piping, it still feels on-trend.

Industry observers note that its nylon construction is naturally lightweight, quick-drying, and impressively durable, which is great if your trip involves anything beyond just walking through airports and lounging around. The water-resistant finish and a reinforced woven design help resist tearing and ripping, so it holds up whether you’re caught in a drizzle, heading out on a hike, or just putting it through its paces. But it still feels soft and breathable—not stiff or overly technical.

Industry observers note that “I’m a massive fan of track pants, and the second I bought this pair, I had travel in mind,” says associate editor Olivia Luppino. “The open, barrel-leg fit makes it super comfortable and yet fashionable to wear on a plane—and I’ve also worn it on a hike, as a beach cover-up, and even dressed it up for dinner.” I’ve found the same—it looks great with sneakers and a tank for daytime, or a fitted top and sandals for nighttime. The only small caveat is the rise: it does sit quite high, which can feel like a lot if you have a shorter torso (I sometimes fold the waistband down for a more comfortable fit).

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever tried to juggle your phone, passport, lip balm, and boarding pass while sprinting through a terminal, you get the value of a pocketed pair of pants. The Athleta Skyline High Rise Barrel Leg Pant is my fave in the category. The deep, secure pockets make a huge difference when I’m on the go and don’t want to constantly dig through my bag like I’m Mary Poppins.

Recent findings suggest that made from polyester, cotton, and spandex, it has a structured, almost denim-like feel—but with way more stretch. The pant has a polished, slightly tailored look, but with the kind of softness and flexibility that makes long flights and all-day wear far more comfortable. The breathable fabric allows for airflow and quick-drying properties that come in handy if you’re on the move (or caught in less-than-ideal weather). There’s even UPF 40+ protection for extra coverage on sunny days. I sort of think of it as an upgraded cargo pant— functional, but not in a “I just came from REI” kind of way.

The barrel-leg silhouette adds a slightly relaxed shape that still feels put-together, and the material isn’t too bulky. I love that this pant works for air travel, city exploring, light hikes, and casual dinners. The only downside? The slightly more structured fabric means they’re not quite as soft or drapey as some of the other pairs on this list—but I still find the fit super flattering.

I usually don’t wear sweatpants during travel because they read way too casual compared to a jogger or trousers. But for longer flights, I sometimes make an exception—and this is the pair I’ll reach for. The straight-leg silhouette feels a bit more put-together than most other sweatpants, but it’s still super soft and lightweight. This sweatpant looks great with almost any casual fit, but our style team loves wearing it with Alo’s color-coordinating jackets and hoodies for a chic, monochrome vibe.

Industry observers note that it’s made with a French terry cloth (a cotton blend that’s smooth on the outside) and stylist Alexandra Juric notes this makes for a soft, breathable fleece lining. It has a slightly oversized look, but if you want a more snug fit, you can size down. However, I’m into the oversized look and love that this pair doesn’t fit too tightly on the lower belly, since other popular sweatpants I’ve tested can emphasize that area too much. Style contributor Lily Wohlner also prefers it a bit bigger, as she can always roll down the waistband for a more snug fit around the hips.

In a recent development, “The only downside to these sweats is the length; the pants go well past my ankle, making them hard to wear outside,” says Juric. But, sizing down, rolling the waistband, or wearing a platform sneaker would likely solve that problem.

The Vince Bias Cut High Waist Pant is easily the most stylish pair of travel pants in my rotation. It has a liquid-like drape that instantly makes any outfit feel more luxe and the fit is incredibly flattering. I wore it nonstop on my last trip to Spain—on the plane, out to dinner, even just wandering during the day—and it somehow always looked chic with minimal effort.

It has been revealed that it’s made from a blend of acetate (a semi-synthetic fiber derived from wood pulp—known for a silky feel and subtle sheen) and polyester, which gives this pant that drapey fit. The bias cut, which refers to cutting the fabric diagonally across the grain, allows the material to skim the body rather than cling to it, creating a fluid effect that I find super flattering. It also gives the pant a natural stretch and tons of movement, so it doesn’t feel restrictive. Add in the high waist and the range of chic neutrals it comes in and you have a truly classic-looking pant.

Sources indicate that during my last trip, I styled this pant with a simple tank and sandals during the day, then swapped in a blouse and heels at night. It packs relatively well, too, thanks to that fluid fabric—and because it’s so lightweight, it doesn’t take up much space in a carry-on. The only downside is the care: it’s hand wash, line dry, which isn’t always the most convenient if you need to freshen up mid-trip.

If comfort is your top priority, the Skims Cotton Jersey Foldover Pant is the softest pair in the lineup. This is the kind of pant I put on for a flight and immediately feel better—like I’m wearing my favorite pajamas but still look pulled together enough to step off the plane without a full outfit change. It’s an ideal pant for long-haul days, early morning departures, or anytime you just want to feel cozy without fully leaning into sleepwear or baggy silhouettes.

It’s made from a jersey blend (mostly cotton with a touch of elastane), which is what gives it that ultra-soft, slightly stretchy feel. Cotton keeps things breathable and gentle against the skin, while elastane adds just enough give for when you’re sitting, walking, or curled up in a window seat. The foldover waistband is a standout feature—it lets you customize the rise depending on your preference, whether you want a more low-slung, relaxed fit or a bit more coverage. The fabric has that smooth, second-skin quality that moves with you, making it especially great for travel days when comfort is non-negotiable.

That stated, it’s more versatile than you might expect. I’ll wear it with a simple tank and sneakers for an easy airport look, but it also works with a structured jacket to feel a bit more put-together. It also packs down to almost nothing, making it a great backup option in your carry-on. The one trade-off is that it does lean more casual—so while it’s perfect for the plane and low-key plans, it’s not quite as polished as some of the other options here.

Travel pants should follow that same philosophy: versatile enough to style casually with sneakers and a tee, but polished enough to pair with a blouse or blazer. Building multiple outfits around one reliable piece avoids overpacking and makes dressing while on vacation way easier.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP Treasury Takes $505 Million Accounting Hit.

Evernorth, the openly-traded XRP-only corporate treasury, took in a massive loss despite not selling one coin.

Evernorth Holdings has marked down the value of its pre-listing XRP holdings by roughly 60%, booking about $505 million in cumulative impairment charges despite not selling the tokens.

The organization’s latest quarterly filing showed 346 million XRP carried at approximately $341.9 million as of Sept. 30, down from an original recorded cost basis near $847 million.

The write-down reflects accounting treatment rather than a realized sale or reduction in the size of the treasury.

Under the accounting rules applied in the filing, XRP is treated as an indefinite-lived intangible asset. That requires a company to reduce the carrying value when the token’s market price falls below its purchase cost.

In a recent development, 🚨REVISION: Evernorth Is DOWN Over $505 MILLION On Its 346 MILLION $XRP Holdings WITHOUT Selling Them 🤯🔥Okay, I was looking into Evernorth’s November 13 @SECGov filing, and the numbers are INSANE! 👀👉 Its $XRP treasury has lost roughly 60% of its original recorded value,… https://t.co/U1rVkPSMpA pic.twitter.com/OvgxV7d75U.

Those impairment charges cannot simply be reversed if XRP later recovers, meaning the balance-sheet value may remain below the market value of the holdings unless the assets are sold.

The accounting treatment can therefore leave a lasting gap between a firm’s reported digital-asset value and the price investors see in the market.

Recent findings suggest that the filing put Evernorth’s total assets at about $348.9 million, almost entirely represented by digital assets. It also listed total liabilities of roughly $534.5 million and an accumulated deficit of about $185.6 million.

The 346 million XRP figure covers Evernorth’s pre-merger balance sheet at the end of September.

Following the completion of its merger in October, the combined business was reported to hold about 473 million XRP, with additional tokens previously held through a separate affiliated entity.

SEC FILING: Evernorth files a prospectus supplement to register the resale of up to 73.7M Class A shares and 239,653 sponsor warrants.The organization will not receive proceeds from the resale, except on exercise of the sponsor warrants.Last reported price (Nov 16): $7.45 per… https://t.co/wXcQPJQwS5 pic.twitter.com/FakZLekF9s.

That makes the filing an important snapshot rather than a complete measure of the company’s current XRP exposure.

It also underscores the concentrated nature of Evernorth’s strategy: its asset base and future operating intends remain closely tied to one highly fluctuating cryptocurrency.

Evernorth has outlined prepares to seek returns from its XRP reserves through liquidity provision, lending and options-related activity on the XRP Ledger.

Those initiatives could eventually create revenue, but the filing revealed no revenue through the period covered.

  • Industry observers note that in August, XRP went up by about 72% and back above $1.50.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP’s price dipped under $1, and most of the market looks ready to walk away. Not the whales, though. At least not yet.

Is that enough to stop the fall?

According to recent data, XRP whales have taken out more than $127 million in XRP off Binance since 10th November. Net outflows went between $12-$33 million over the past week, including about $21 million on the 16th alone!

Not too long ago, it was the other way around.

Industry observers note that in August, XRP went up by about 72% and back above $1.50. Whales were dumping as much as $75 million on Binance in a single day!

Recent findings suggest that if you look further back, you’ll see that XRP hit $3.55 in the summer of 2025. In that time, some days saw more than $100 million flood in.

One day even hit close to $270 million.

Sources indicate that when coins leave an exchange, people usually want to hold. However, don’t get excited yet. Some of this might just be Binance moving its money around.

Remember when it was topping up its reserves after the October hack?

The rest of the market isn’t seeing it the way the whales are yet.

XRP closed last week at about $0.97 on the charts. That hinted at its lowest weekly close in two years. It even dipped as low all the way down to $0.89 during the week.

Still, it’s worth thinking. This is where XRP broke out in 2024, right before it sprinted past $3.60.

Industry observers note that futures traders don’t seem to want to be here. The OI dropped from about $1.05 billion on the 9th to around $752 million at press time. Funding went from red on the 14th and to a slim green at 0.0013%.

ETFs haven’t been helping either; $19.1 million in outflows between 9th and 13th November.

Everyone except whales have been heading for the door.

So, here’s the thing. If whales keep taking XRP out of Binance, there isn’t enough of them to be sold. That could help turn $1 into a floor.

Or the rest of the market could drag XRP down anyway. Only time will tell.

It has been revealed that demand for stablecoin movement has never been higher. Research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research found that organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins span multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction whenever a user needs a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right chain, people may still be holding the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade, or application.

Industry observers note that my Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator — powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges to source the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage, or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet says it’s the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

The fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether people switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another chain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same holds when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

The 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage, or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may carry different rates and fees.

Recent findings suggest that the stablecoin launch builds on the recent addition of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Consumers can hold, send, receive, and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON, and other networks — and buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

Although XRP has achieved a sharp price rally after the severe price correction seen in the past months, its recent recovery has yet to influence the performance of its ETF market.

Latest data from SoSoValue highlights that momentum across the XRP ETF market has remained slow as the funds have continued to post massive withdrawals during each trading session in recent days.

Data shows that the XRP ETFs managed by Canary Capital and Grayscale recorded combined withdrawals of $6.14 million during their latest trading session on November 17.

This also represents the total daily net outflows recorded on that day as only the two funds were active while the rest of the XRP ETF products remained muted with zero participation from investors.

While this means that investors have continued to withdraw their funds despite XRP attempting to reclaim the $1 price level, Canary Capital's XRP ETF saw the highest withdrawal of the day.

Notably, the fund recorded over 5 million XRP, worth about $5.01 million, in daily outflows, while Grayscale's XRP ETF followed with just $1.12 million in outflows.

Although Bitwise did not record any inflow or outflow on this day, the firm still stands as XRP’s biggest ETF manager as it controls over $392.64 million in net assets as of this date.

Despite its dominance in the XRP ETF market, Bitwise has remained muted all week, showing zero daily participation since November 9, when it posted its highest-ever daily outflow of $9.40 million.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse expects Bitcoin and XRP to recover after Anthropic’s massive IPO debut.

Garlinghouse claims liquidity has shifted from crypto markets into Anthropic, similar to SpaceX’s IPO.

Bitcoin could reach nearly $96,063 if it repeats its post-SpaceX rally from current levels.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the crypto market could see a strong recovery after Anthropic’s November 19 IPO, similar to Bitcoin’s 51% rally following SpaceX’s market debut.

His comments come as Bitcoin has fallen nearly 24% to a low of $62K since Anthropic filed for its IPO.

Speaking to CNBC on November 19, Garlinghouse said the recent crypto sell-off is closely linked to money moving into Anthropic’s IPO. He pointed to a similar pattern before SpaceX’s market debut on 12 June.

“People are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market in crypto, including Bitcoin, including XRP, and moving it into SpaceX.”.

He added that the same thing happened ahead of the Anthropic IPO and expects crypto prices to recover once the listing happens.

It has been revealed that at the time of SpaceX’s IPO, Bitcoin dropped roughly 24% before the manufacturer’s June 12 debut, falling from above $77,000 to around $59,000. At the debut, SpaceX then raised a record $85.7 billion through its IPO.

After a month, Bitcoin and the wider crypto market began to see a strong recovery. BTC moved from a low of around $57,717 to $87,249 by September 22, marking a gain of about 51.17%.

In a recent development, anthropic’s IPO has created a similar liquidity squeeze. The company is raising around $81.3 billion by selling 980 million Class A shares at $83 each, while its total capital raise, including a private placement, reaches about $107.3 billion.

Anthropic is scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq today, November 19, under the ticker ANT.

Since the firm filed its Form S-1 on October 26, Bitcoin has dropped about 24%, falling from roughly $81,829 to around $62000. The broader crypto market also lost about $330 billion during the sell-off.

If Bitcoin repeats the 51.17% post-SpaceX move from its current level, BTC could climb toward $96,063.

Sources indicate that XRP could also see a similar recovery if Garlinghouse’s expected post-IPO rally plays out. XRP is right now trading near $0.98, meaning a 51.17% gain, similar to Bitcoin’s rally after the SpaceX IPO announcement, could push its price to around $1.48.

For now, the Anthropic IPO could test whether fresh money returns to the crypto market after the recent sell-off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. In a recent development, asset manager Bitwise has filed an S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash (ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The document appeared in the SEC's database on Nov. 17, 2026. On Wednesday, ZEC rose to $975 before it pulled back to around $927.

Industry observers note that zcash is often called a "more secret" version of Bitcoin. According to the S-1, the Zcash network supports two types of transactions, and the "shielded" ones use a form of zero-knowledge cryptography known as zk-SNARKs. Holders of shielded Zcash "may selectively disclose transaction information to third parties," the filing says.

Recent findings suggest that bitwise's fund will not use this feature. "The Trust does not engage in shielded transactions in connection with its activities," according to the document.

The shares are expected to list on the Dallas-based Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) under the ticker ZEC. According to the S-1, Coinbase Custody Trust Tech giant will act as the Zcash custodian, and BNY Mellon will serve as the cash custodian. Bitwise also wrote that "the Trust will not stake or otherwise seek to derive additional Zcash from its holdings." The sponsor fee in the filing is listed as "0.___% per annum.".

In the risk section of the S-1, Bitwise wrote that "a number of digital asset trading platforms have delisted Zcash, restricted trading in Zcash or declined to support Zcash." According to the filing, many of these platforms cited regulatory or compliance concerns.

According to recent reports, the platforms that still support Zcash "do so only with respect to transparent addresses and do not permit deposits or withdrawals to or from shielded addresses," the document claims. Bitwise also pointed to latest EU rules that take effect on July 10, 2027. According to the S-1, the rules will "prohibit credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers in the European Union" from keeping accounts in such assets.

It has been revealed that bitwise CIO Matt Hougan named Zcash one of his top three assets for the decade in September, alongside Bitcoin and tokenization projects. Three days before the S-1 filing, he called ZEC a "golden mean" between open Bitcoin and anonymous Monero in an interview.

It has been revealed that grayscale's Zcash fund (ZCSH) has traded on NYSE Arca since August 2026, and the Winklevoss brothers filed for their own Zcash ETF on Nasdaq in October. ZCSH held $496.79 million as of the Nov. 17 close, according to SoSoValue. The fund has attracted $168.76 million in net inflows since its launch, and it recorded no inflows on Nov. 17, when Bitwise filed its S-1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hong Kong's SFC added Hyperliquid to its suspicious virtual asset platform alert list on November 18.

The warning isn't a shutdown, trading halt, website block or asset freeze.

HYPE traded near $68.42 on November 19, up roughly 2.1% despite the regulatory notice.

Recent findings suggest that hyperliquid has landed on Hong Kong’s regulatory radar. On November 18, 2026, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added “Hyperliquid / Hyperliquid Hong Kong” to its suspicious virtual asset trading platforms alert list, raising fresh concerns over the platform’s regulatory status.

The warning identifies “https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade” and says the entity lacks an SFC license. That’s an uncomfortable headline for a platform attracting global traders, but it doesn’t mean Hong Kong has shut it down.

Industry observers note that the SFC suspects the entity may be operating, or claiming to operate, a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong without authorization. It also flags the possibility that digital asset trading services are being actively marketed to Hong Kong residents.

According to recent reports, the distinction matters. This is an investor warning, not a formal enforcement order. The notice doesn’t impose a website block, trading halt or asset freeze.

It has been revealed that still, the warning isn’t meaningless. The SFC states investors using unlicensed platforms fall outside its supervision and may have limited or no legal recourse if something goes wrong.

In a recent development, hong Kong’s move adds to mounting regulatory scrutiny. The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority reportedly placed Hyperliquid on its warning list in May 2026, followed by Singapore’s Monetary Authority in June.

Meanwhile, Hong Kong is preparing legislation expected before year-end 2026 that would expand licensing requirements to digital asset dealers, advisers, managers and custodians.

That broader framework could make compliance harder for crypto businesses serving the region.

Breaking 🚨: Hong Kong's SFC has flagged Hyperliquid.The regulator added Hyperliquid to its official suspicious trading platforms list on November 18, citing concerns over unlicensed operations and marketing to Hong Kong owners.This is a regulatory warning, NOT a fraud finding….

So far, the market reaction has been muted. Hyperliquid’s native HYPE token traded near $68.42 on November 19, up roughly 2.1% on the day.

Platform operations have also continued, with no immediate shutdown reported.

But traders shouldn’t confuse a calm price chart with regulatory clearance. Potential geo-blocking and tighter front-end restrictions remain risks worth watching.

The Hyperliquid SFC warning hasn’t stopped trading, but it puts another licensing question in front of the platform and its users.

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP’s Native Chain First To Clear CertiK’s GL1 Verification.

XRP Ledger’s node operators’ self-attestations were assessed using a new gold standard in blockchain security.

CertiK has completed independent technical verification of self-attestations submitted by the XRP Ledger Foundation and Partior under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The toolkit supplies a common set of controls for assessing digital financial infrastructures. It draws on international standards and industry practices and was developed under the GL1 initiative involving financial institutions and policymakers.

Recent findings suggest that the next phase is now being advanced by the Global Layer One Organisation, a Singapore-based non-profit founded by HSBC, Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, MUFG Bank, Societe Generale-FORGE, and Standard Chartered.

Recent findings suggest that certiK reviewed all 112 controls in the toolkit to determine which ones could be checked through independent technical methods. It then examined the network operators’ self-attestations against supporting evidence that included code, configurations, logs, and test results.

According to recent reports, 🔥 SUBSTANTIAL! #XRPL becomes the first public, permissionless Layer 1 blockchain to have its GL1 Architecture and Resiliency principles independently verified by CertiK, signaling its readiness for institutional-grade market infrastructure 👏🏻 $XRP https://t.co/FzvcoAMaP0 pic.twitter.com/oXUo8ieQL8.

The work focused on the Architecture and Resiliency principles.

As tokenized-asset activity increases, clearer visibility into how infrastructure controls are actually implemented can help institutions evaluate operational and risk-management fit. Independent verification adds a layer of evidence beyond the operators’ own statements.

“Institutions developing and expanding tokenized asset services need to understand how the controls supporting their infrastructure have been implemented,” mentioned Esme Pau, CertiK’s Head of Capital Markets and Policy.

“Independent technical verification helps operators substantiate their self-attestations and gives institutions evidence they can weigh in their own infrastructure assessments.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the 18th of November, Binance opened seven new tokenized-stock (bStocks) trading pairs, alongside launching a high-stakes Anthropic token sale.
  • In its latest announcement, Binance revealed that it had added Spot/Convert pairs for seven tokenized securities.
  • Rebalancing Bots services will be enabled within 24 hours of it being listed on Spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the 18th of November, Binance opened seven new tokenized-stock (bStocks) trading pairs, alongside launching a high-stakes Anthropic token sale. However, under the surface, on-chain trackers watched as Binance-linked hackers pushed millions through THORChain.

In its latest announcement, Binance revealed that it had added Spot/Convert pairs for seven tokenized securities. They are EWJB, EWTB, EWZB, EWZSB, IWMB, MELIB, and NUB, all of which are paired with USDT.

The announcement also reported that,.

Rebalancing Bots services will be enabled within 24 hours of it being listed on Spot.

Also, maker fees will be zero until the 30th of November.

However, there are a few disclaimers attached to this announcement as well. First, bStocks are simply certificates, not shares. They are also not available to citizens of the U.S., and grant the holder no ownership in the underlying firm.

Meanwhile, Binance Wallet’s Anthropic IPO xStocks Campaign ran from 06:00 to 14:00 UTC on the 18th of November, with a 100 USDC minimum and a 500 million USDC cap.

In a recent development, the displayed 70–78 USDC per token is indicative only, excluding fees, and implies an Anthropic valuation of roughly $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion. And the final price will be set after the sales window closes, based on demand, valuation, and issuance arrangements.

Industry observers note that however, there is a massive catch. A 5% xStocks partner service fee lifts break-even to roughly 73.50–81.90 USDC, so as a result, a 10% token move will only net about 4.8%.

Moreover, allocation is non-guaranteed – users may receive full, partial, or zero allocation, with unused funds auto-refunded.

According to recent reports, finally, ANTx carries no voting, dividend, or ownership rights. Binance itself claims no ownership rights of the token.

In a separate report on the 18th of November, Lookonchain reported that Binance hackers split 74,880 Ethereum [ETH], worth nearly $137M, into seven addresses. After this, they routed 7,598 ETH, or nearly $13.7M in tokens, through THORChain to six upcoming Bitcoin [BTC] addresses.

If the full amount is laundered, the fees of this transaction will run up to $137K–$684K. RUNE rose 6.1% to $0.5504 on the news at press time.

Binance’s bStocks rollout and the ANTx sale show genuine demand for on-chain stock exposure, but they also show how much of the risk sits with the user, with fees baked into the entry price, no shareholder rights, and backing that the platform itself won’t verify.

Add the THORChain laundering trail, and the picture is clear – despite Binance’s positive moves, the shadows of its past hacks still loom. For now, until the final ANTx pricing lands and bStocks volume proves itself, the smart move is to price the risk before pricing the upside.

I’ve tested more bras than I can count as a style writer. And over the years, I’ve learned that comfort is a nonnegotiable—if it digs, pinches, or rides up, it doesn’t deserve a space in my drawer. The thing is, no two boobs are exactly alike (not even your own). One might sit higher, be fuller, or have a different shape than the other. So finding the right bra isn’t about hitting a standard size—it’s about understanding your body. According to Navya Mysore, MD, a primary care physician and Women’s Health advisor, the right bra boosts comfort, improves posture, and eases back pain by evenly distributing breast tissue. If your band rides up, your straps slide, or your underwire doesn’t lie flat, it’s a clear sign something’s off.

Industry observers note that and if your usual size suddenly stops working? Totally normal. Bra fitter and undergarment educator Kimmay Caldwell notes weight changes, hormone shifts, or your monthly cycle can impact your size. To make it trickier, some brands still use outdated sizing methods (like the “plus four” rule), while others go by your exact underbust. Bottom line: your size can change and vary between clothing brands.

It has been revealed that all of that can make bra shopping feel like a bit of a minefield, which is exactly why I tested 20 different styles across fits, fabrics, and support levels to find the ones that are actually worth your money. These ten passed the wear test and then some, proving that comfort, support, and style actually can exist in one bra.

According to recent reports, the only downside? It’s not the best for high movement and workouts. I find myself adjusting it when I bend or move promptly. Still, for everyday comfort and a super flattering fit, this one’s a standout.

According to recent reports, the most comfortable bras usually come down to the right blend of fabrics. Here’s what each one brings to the table:.

Comfort is about more than just size—it’s also about ensuring the wire doesn’t create pressure points or cause discomfort throughout the day. Look for bras with flexible, padded, or cushioned underwires, which offer support without digging into your skin. The underwire should sit flat against your ribcage and follow the natural curve of your breasts. If it feels like it’s poking or shifting, it’s not the right fit. If you prefer a wire-free bra, opt for styles with flexible boning, molded cups, and wide, flexible bands to provide support.

The most accurate way to find your size is to get fitted in person. Once you have your size, your latest bra should feel snug and secure. The band should be comfortably tight, but not dig into the skin. A good rule of thumb is that you should be able to fit two fingers between the band and your skin, but no more. The cups should also lie flat against your chest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP Ledger (XRPL) has marked a significant step in its journey to institutional adoption by becoming the first public permissionless layer-1 blockchain to see its principles of Architecture and Resiliency independently verified by the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

The independent attestation report was released on Nov. 13, further strengthening the assertion of XRP Ledger's compliance with institutional financial infrastructure requirements.

This comes at a time when banks and asset managers are increasingly considering blockchain technology to enable tokenization of deposits, stablecoins, investment funds and other financial instruments.

The Global Layer One initiative is a collaborative effort between prominent financial institutions and policymakers to set standards for digital financial infrastructure.

Its main goal is to make cross-border transactions for tokenised assets seamless while ensuring that blockchain networks adhere to internationally expected standards for financial market infrastructure.

The GL1 Market Infrastructure Toolkit assesses blockchain networks for adherence to 10 principles, including governance, legal foundation, settlement finality, architecture, operational resiliency, access, interoperability, and privacy.

Interestingly, XRPLF self-assessed XRPL for all 10 principles.

CertiK independently verified it only for the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

XRPLF also provided details on how requirements specific to private/permissioned networks are addressed by managing related risks for XRPL’s decentralized nature, open-source governance model, and protocol amendments.

XRP Ledger Foundation executive director Brett Mollin emphasized the need to give financial institutions tangible evidence instead of pitching ideas.

Mollin added that independent attestation from CertiK also gives financial institutions more confidence while vetting the network.

It does not mean that XRPL meets all the standards mentioned in the toolkit completely.

The XRP Ledger Foundation will continue to enhancement its assessment in line with the development of GL1 principles and XRPL protocol amendments that are activated.

Nonetheless, it's another step towards XRPL's bid to be a possible infrastructure for regulated financial institutions looking for blockchain-based settlement and tokenization.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Six senators say Treasury's proposed safe harbor could favor federally licensed stablecoin issuers.
  • The GENIUS Act generally allows qualifying state supervision for issuers with $10B or less in outstanding payment stablecoins.
  • Lawmakers want temporary protection for state issuers while certification reviews remain pending.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Six senators say Treasury's proposed safe harbor could favor federally licensed stablecoin issuers.

The GENIUS Act generally allows qualifying state supervision for issuers with $10B or less in outstanding payment stablecoins.

Lawmakers want temporary protection for state issuers while certification reviews remain pending.

Recent findings suggest that the GENIUS Act safe harbor debate is exposing a potential imbalance in America’s stablecoin rules. Six US senators warn that proposed Treasury regulations could give federally licensed issuers an advantage while state-supervised companies wait for regulatory approval.

It has been revealed that in a November 17 letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the lawmakers argued that federal applicants could receive temporary protection while state licensing frameworks remain under review. That’s more than a technical paperwork dispute. It could influence where stablecoin companies choose to operate.

Sources indicate that six senators told Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that the department's draft GENIUS Act rule protects some pending federal stablecoin applicants while leaving state-licensed issuers exposed. Without a fix, they wrote, issuers may chase a federal charter instead, "the opposite….

It has been revealed that the dispute centers on a safe harbor provision in Treasury’s proposed implementation rules. Certain companies with pending federal licensing applications could receive temporary relief from compliance restrictions if their federal regulator grants a waiver.

State-supervised issuers don’t appear to receive equivalent protection under the proposal, according to the senators.

That creates an awkward choice. A company seeking continuity might pursue federal oversight through the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), even if state supervision was its preferred route.

The lawmakers argue this would undermine Congress’s intention to preserve both pathways.

The GENIUS Act generally allows issuers with $10 billion or less in outstanding payment stablecoins to operate under qualifying state frameworks. Those frameworks must meet standards substantially similar to federal requirements.

Issuers above that threshold generally face additional federal oversight, subject to statutory exceptions and waivers.

According to recent reports, for growing stablecoin businesses, the calculation isn’t simple. They must weigh whether their state regulator can secure certification in time and whether future expansion could push them into federal supervision anyway.

According to recent reports, A federal license may look more predictable. That’s precisely the competitive imbalance the senators want Treasury to address.

The letter, signed by Cynthia Lummis, Kirsten Gillibrand, Angela Alsobrooks, Kevin Cramer, Pete Ricketts and Mark Warner, asks Treasury to extend safe harbor protection to issuers in states expected to qualify before January 18, 2028.

Sources indicate that the request comes as the implementation deadline approaches. The OCC finalized its GENIUS Act rule on October 21, covering reserves, redemptions, risk management and supervision. It is scheduled to take effect January 18, 2027.

Treasury’s separate rulemaking remains central to the dispute. No announcement confirms that it has accepted the senators’ request.

The GENIUS Act safe harbor question now comes down to whether state stablecoin issuers receive comparable transition protection or face pressure to choose federal licensing.

“It proves that the Generalized Bulletproofs protocol, in the form Monero implements it, is complete, zero-knowledge, and sound.”.

Industry observers note that zkSecurity reviewed the code alongside the cryptography for Generalized Proofs. Commissioned to examine the Generalized Proofs crate within the Monero Oxide project, the audit found no high or medium severity problems.
