📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on Nov. 18 with seven recommendations on the draft documents CP26/36 and GC26/7. Three of them concern CP26/36, and four concern GC26/7. The letter was signed by HPC chief executive Jake Chervinsky.

The UK's newly introduced crypto regime will start to apply on Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA opened its window for crypto license applications on Sept. 30, 2026, and the window will close on Feb. 28, 2027.

According to the letter, "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity." HPC argued that attaching obligations to a person who could not discharge them "would offer consumers no additional protection.".

In the letter, HPC also compared public blockchains with the internet. "Like a public blockchain, the internet depends on protocols that identifiable persons maintain and upgrade over time," the group wrote.

HPC asked the FCA to assess each participant in a blockchain network separately. Proprietary traders and market makers "supply much of the liquidity on which order books depend," the group wrote. HPC also asked the regulator to describe compliance requirements as outcomes and to hold regulated firms accountable for them.

According to recent reports, on Aug. 24, HPC urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to harmonize their rules for perpetual contracts. The group argued that such products should be classified by their economic structure. According to HPC, a harmonized framework would let exchanges compete on "execution quality and liquidity.".

On Sept. 30, HPC sent its response to the European Union's review of the MiCA rules. In it, the group asked the EU to treat crypto perpetual futures as derivatives under MiFID II. "Clarity in application, rather than newly introduced legislation, is what would assist in regulating perpetual futures," HPC wrote at the time.

Chervinsky previously served as chief policy officer at the Blockchain Association and as chief legal officer at the crypto venture firm Variant.

As Bitcoin prices fell, the net realized losses grew, indicative of investors selling at greater losses. This behavior is commonly seen during bear market phases.

Increased liquidations hastened the perpetuals futures demand contraction, and bearish market sentiment meant the combined total demand growth metric’s 30-day average was -400k BTC.

There were few buyers to absorb the supply being sold.

Industry observers note that bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has once again predicted that Strategy will be forced to sell its Bitcoin stash to defend the unrealistic yields of its controversial STRC stock. Schiff, known for his crypto-skeptic tweets, has again noted STRC is under pressure after total BTC holdings plummeted more than $10 billion in value following the latest market squeeze.

Schiff highlighted that even with the latest buyback programs, STRC is likely to face further pressure and, eventually, Strategy will be forced to burn through its cash reserves, including USDT and then Bitcoin itself. The only alternative, he suggests, is to raise or suspend the dividend, which will tank the stock price and send the whole Saylor initiative further down the abyss.

In a recent development, STRC is a variable-yield perpetual preferred stock issued by Strategy, which is the largest corporate Bitcoin holder. The stock was used to raise funds to fuel Saylor’s aggressive BTC buying strategy. The shares are designed to trade near $100, with monthly adjustments based on their dividend rate, which is currently as high as 12% and paid daily.

While Bitcoin proponents initially welcomed Saylor’s flamboyant approach, they have generally become skeptical of the complex offering because of its risk and complexity. CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju, among others, has criticized it over the years. He believes that Saylor has made a habit of buying the digital currency at relative highs, putting STRC under further pressure. It has become a running joke that whenever Saylor buys, it marks a relative top and a sign for short-term traders to sell.

Here is the graph of all Strategy BTC buys:.

Recent Strategy buys confirm this unfortunate Saylor trend of buying BTC at its relative highs. It is not Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) by any stretch of imagination, as STRC comes under pressure with each dip, and Saylor simply doesn’t have enough funds to purchase the crypto at that time.

So, Schiff is by no means an isolated critic of the STRC stock. The move has invited criticism from the industry’s own players. However, Schiff is connecting STRC directly to BTC, even though it is a corporate decision and has no relation to the decentralized cryptocurrency’s ecosystem. He has predicted the fall of the top cryptocurrency by market capitalization for most of the last 13 years. However, this time he could be proven right, as BTC remains in relative free fall, and with each dip, STRC drops into deeper trouble.

Home » Crypto Market News » Google Warns North Korean Hackers Are Poisoning AI Tools to Drain Crypto Firms.

State-backed hackers are using fake recruiters and tampered Claude Code settings to breach crypto networks.

Cyberattacks against the cryptocurrency industry have crossed a dangerous threshold as threat actors shift from basic AI prompts to autonomous AI agents capable of running intrusions from start to finish.

According to the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant report, state-backed hackers are actively targeting crypto firms in North America and Europe by turning popular AI developer tools into malware delivery traps.

It has been revealed that researchers have linked a suspected North Korean hacking campaign to attacks on cryptocurrency companies. The group, known as Midnight Neptune, uses fake recruiter profiles and tampered software settings to break into company networks.

The attackers approach targets on professional networking platforms, posing as recruiters with AI-generated profile photos.

Industry observers note that they then invite victims to fake online meetings, where simulated audio or video problems prompt them to run scripts to fix the issue. This social engineering trick, known as ClickFix, gets victims to execute malicious commands themselves.

Once inside a company’s network, the attackers tamper with its internal code repositories, modifying the configuration file used by Anthropic’s Claude Code.

The next time a developer debuts Claude Code, the altered settings silently download a backdoor called SOMBERMEME.

The attackers also create GitHub Personal Access Tokens disguised as Microsoft Copilot to make their activity look like normal developer traffic.

The report also revealed a major advance in automated hacking that puts open-source Web3 infrastructure at risk.

Google researchers discovered an active tool called exploit_agent on an exposed testing server. It uses large language models (LLMs) to compare software code before and after security updates, identify newly patched vulnerabilities, write code to exploit them, and launch attacks — all without human involvement.

It has been revealed that that puts open-source protocols at risk. Since code updates are publicly available, hackers can spot newly fixed vulnerabilities and exploit them before operators have a chance to install the patches. Even a brief delay can leave networks vulnerable.

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported that disclosed vulnerabilities and exploits nearly doubled between January and August 2026.

Exploited zero-day vulnerabilities also rose from an average of eight per month in 2025 to 11 in 2026, reaching 22 in August alone.

Beyond traditional cyberattacks, Mandiant warns of a growing threat called LLMJacking. Criminals hijack corporate cloud accounts, steal AI computing power, and resell it through underground marketplaces known as LLM Mixers. The resulting fraud can exceed $100,000 in a single day and reach $1 million per victim.

Meanwhile, influence networks use more than 100,000 fake social media accounts to spread misinformation, fuel token hype, and trigger artificial market panic.

To counter these threats, Google is deploying AI security tools such as Major Sleep and CodeMender to find and fix software vulnerabilities before hackers exploit them.

The GTIG report highlights several security risks for the crypto industry.

Companies using AI coding tools should check their code repositories for unauthorized commands and keep third-party access tokens secure.

They also need to install software updates swiftly, as AI-powered hackers can turn newly discovered vulnerabilities into working attacks.

Employees should never follow unexpected browser or video-call instructions asking them to copy and run computer commands.

Investors, meanwhile, should be cautious of sudden waves of online hype or panic, which fake social media accounts can create at scale.

Tech Report: Gonka AI Hit by $1 Million Exploit as Hacker Drains Stablecoins

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and issue Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and issue unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.

According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and issue Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.

Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.

Combined, the total value of the affected assets stood at around $1.06 million, per Onchain Lens.

Following the hack, the funds were transferred through the decentralized exchange Uniswap and multiple crypto wallets, making it challenging to trace their final destination.

Industry observers note that the attack targeted Gonka AI's cross-chain bridge. The cross-chain bridge makes it possible to transfer assets from Gonka AI's native chain to Ethereum and vice versa.

According to the project's technical documentation, withdrawing funds from Gonka to Ethereum requires certain cryptographic signatures from the network's validator set.

The cryptographic signatures are checked against the BLS group key, which changes with every network epoch.

Per the report, the attacker was able to change the epoch BLS group key on the bridge, making it possible for the hacker to control the part of the bridge responsible for authorizing fund withdrawals.

Thus, the hacker was able to withdraw funds from the bridge's stablecoin reserves and issue WGNK tokens without locking the required amount of assets on the native blockchain.

Blockchain security firm Blockaid noted that the hack had taken place, with the total amount of funds stolen reaching about $1.05 million across roughly five transactions at the time of the initial alert.

At the time it spotted the suspicious activity, Blockaid noted that the hack was still ongoing.

Onchain Lens's numbers differ slightly, with the firm reporting around $884,800 in stablecoin withdrawals and $172,000 in unbacked WGNK issuance.

Notably, the issuance of unbacked tokens presents an additional problem, given that such tokens could potentially enter circulation without the necessary reserves to back them.

Could Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO help revive crypto? Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse thinks the listing could remove pressure from digital assets, but his theory needs something more convincing than timing.

Speaking to CNBC, Garlinghouse suggested investors may have sold cryptocurrency to free up capital for Anthropic’s November 19 market debut. The catch? There’s no evidence establishing that connection.

Anthropic priced 980 million Class A shares at $83 each, representing approximately $81.3 billion in total share value. The offering included shares sold by both the company and existing shareholders.

Industry observers note that not all that money goes to Anthropic. Existing investors sold 23.65 million shares, and the firm won’t receive proceeds from those sales.

The stock began trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT on November 19, after pricing above its marketed range of $70 to $78.

That demonstrates substantial demand for AI exposure. It doesn’t reveal whether buyers funded their purchases by selling crypto, equities or other assets.

Bitcoin dropped toward $62,000 on November 18 before recovering above $63,000 early the next day.

Industry observers note that garlinghouse compared the situation with the recovery following SpaceX’s June public listing. His argument is that major IPOs can temporarily absorb investment capital before liquidity returns elsewhere.

That explanation makes intuitive sense, yet it overlooks bigger market drivers.

In a recent development, interest-rate expectation, institutional fund flows, derivatives positioning and broader liquidity conditions also influence crypto prices. Blaming one IPO for market weakness ignores those moving parts.

Sources indicate that the post-listing test is whether investment demand actually improves. US spot Bitcoin ETF flows can reveal changes in institutional demand, while futures activity offers another view of market positioning.

Neither indicator proves that Anthropic investors are returning money to crypto.

Garlinghouse’s Anthropic IPO crypto rebound theory remains plausible, but unverified. Until spot demand, ETF inflows and liquidity strengthen, the listing is a possible explanation for selling pressure not a confirmed catalyst for recovery.

  • In his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov.
  • The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.

In his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov. 18 notice issued by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC). The notice urges rental car services to be cautious about unnecessarily storing images of driver’s licenses and other government-issued identification documents.

The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.

In a recent development, the incident began when the company noticed suspicious activity on its system on Sept. 25. As a result, it launched an investigation into whether someone had accessed its systems without permission, potentially exposing customer data.

Industry observers note that as per the disclosure by Park24 on Oct. 23, about 6.63 million customer accounts were impacted by the breach.

Worse, the investigation uncovered evidence that hackers had transmitted 1,464,800 encrypted images of identification documents, including driver’s licenses, to external locations.

In a recent development, besides that, another 891,602 encrypted images of identification documents were accessed suspiciously. However, investigators found no evidence that these additional ID images had been transmitted outside the organization’s systems.

Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission issued its notice on Nov. 18, focusing on the risks of retaining sensitive personal data even after its original purpose has been fulfilled.

The regulatory body stressed that storing unnecessary identification images could significantly worsen the consequences of cyberattacks.

Although Japan’s latest warning specifically targets the rental car industry, CZ’s decision to share his concerns about this issue also raises questions about personal data protection in the crypto industry.

Generally, centralized crypto exchanges require users to go through a Know Your Customer (KYC) process to access their trading platforms.

Depending on the platform and jurisdiction, these processes may require owners to provide photos of their passports, driver’s licenses, national ID cards, and other sensitive information.

This kind of sensitive data can be a goldmine for cybercriminals, who can exploit stolen personal information for various activities such as identity theft, phishing attacks, fraudulent registrations, and more.

Home » Exchanges » Revolut Lists GoMining Token for UK and European Customers.

The move brings the niche utility token to more than 15 million fintech app users under the EU’s MiCA regulatory framework.

According to recent reports, retail fintech giant Revolut has added GOMINING, the native utility token of the digital Bitcoin mining platform GoMining, to its in-app cryptocurrency trading service. The listing enables over 15 million Revolut crypto customers across the United Kingdom and the European Economic Area (EEA) to buy, hold, and trade the token alongside everyday banking services.

Prior to this integration, GOMINING was primarily accessible through crypto-native exchanges such as Kraken, KuCoin, and Bitget.

Industry observers note that the listing builds on an existing payment integration established in 2024 that allowed European owners to fund GoMining accounts via Revolut Pay. It also adds GOMINING to Revolut’s cryptocurrency trading service.

Recent findings suggest that revolut reviews digital assets before listing them, assessing their risks, compliance requirements and potential financial crime exposure. It also monitors listed tokens on an ongoing basis as part of its procedures under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

Sources indicate that “For years, there has been a clear line between crypto and traditional finance, and most people stayed on one side of it,” stated Mark Zalan, CEO of GoMining, in a statement announcing the listing. “For GoMining, this listing means our token is no longer only for people who already live in the crypto world.”.

Industry observers note that GOMINING has several uses within the GoMining platform. Token holders can use it to pay digital miner maintenance fees, with discounts of up to 20%, buy digital miners on the platform’s marketplace and purchase boosts in Miner Wars, GoMining’s mining game.

Industry observers note that the token also has a governance function. People can lock their GOMINING tokens to receive veGOMINING, which gives them voting rights on the allocation of ecosystem rewards.

Revolut customers can now buy GOMINING directly through the app. To use the token on GoMining, they must first transfer it to an external GoMining account.

According to recent reports, the Revolut listing gives GOMINING exposure to a wider retail audience through a mainstream financial app. It also provides another way for people to acquire the token without first opening an account on a crypto-native exchange.

Sources indicate that however, buying GOMINING through Revolut does not provide direct access to GoMining’s platform features. People must transfer their tokens to an external wallet before using them within the GoMining ecosystem.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit.
  • The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit. This judgement came about after the government failed to prove the brothers made any “material misrepresentation.”.

The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

On a similar note, Ethereum [ETH] co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued that digital assets do not match up to investing in houses. These three developments, when taken together, compound the question of what crypto is actually for.

On the 2nd of April 2023, the brothers seemingly exploited a bug in the MEV-Boost relay software, due to which they could view transactions that sandwich traders believed were private.

The brothers’ alleged proposal for replacement transactions, in turn, resulted in massive losses of roughly $25 million within seconds.

The government called the prosecution,.

Finally, on the 16th of November 2026, Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke, when granting an acquittal, wrote,.

The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos’ conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.

In a recent development, it is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case. Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted.

The court analyzed the government’s theories – including the “lure transactions” and the so-called “false signature,” and found nothing that could support a wire fraud conviction.

A couple of days later, on the 18th of November, Horsley posted on X:.

Rolling bank outages in the AI era – Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.

The post came as thousands of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo customers reported being unable to access their accounts.

Vitalik Buterin, in a separate post on November 18, argued that younger generations have been investing in digital assets over real estate options; doing so, he noted, reduces –.

Perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive.

But he added a condition: housing had the advantage of being –.

A culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.

Industry News: Can AI Hack Smart Contracts? How AI Agents Are Changing Blockchain Security

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: U

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns.
  • Recent findings suggest that for example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period.
  • To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns. However, because an AI agent can iterate and make use of dependencies, local blockchain forks, and decompilation, it weakens the protection gained by keeping source code secret, and can attempt attacks against complex vulnerabilities such as access control bugs, accounting errors, oracle-related bugs and unexpected contract interactions.

Recent findings suggest that for example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period. They were able to reproduce exploits for 207 contracts, totalling $550.1 million (simulated stolen funds).

To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).

Finally, they analysed 2,849 recent smart contracts with no known issues, discovering two previously unknown vulnerabilities that could have resulted in $3,694 (simulated stolen funds), emphasising the ability of AI agents to discover new vulnerabilities rather than simply exploiting known ones.

In a recent development, anthropic emphasised that no actual funds were lost during these experiments. It should also be noted that in one of their experiments using GPT-5, it cost $3,476 for API usage, which leaves a slim (simulated) profit.

With automated hacking becoming more effective, how can we be sure that DeFi will be able to stay ahead of these AI agents? Hacken, a blockchain security firm, reported that $1.18 billion was lost in 107 crypto hacks during the third quarter of 2026. 48% of this was from exploiting smart contracts.

Sources indicate that of course, this doesn’t specify the cause of these hacks. Regardless, it emphasises the importance of being able to stay ahead of AIs which could be used for exploitation.

Sources indicate that chainalysis estimates that approximately $36.7 million was stolen in 2026 from DeFi protocols that had not undergone smart contract verification. It also notes AI-assisted reverse engineering as an emerging risk without attributing any particular thefts to AI.

Industry observers note that in an experiment by a16z on 20 past DeFi price manipulation exploits, apparent success rates of 50% were reduced to 10% when the researchers restricted access to transactional data that revealed the original exploit. When the researchers gave the AI some high-level information about the DeFi domain, success rates jumped to 70%.

In February 2026, OpenAI and Paradigm released a benchmark for evaluating agents’ abilities in the domains of vulnerability detection, patching, and exploitation using an EVM environment (EVMbench). Results showed that GPT-5.3-Codex achieved a 71% success rate in exploitation (limited to a sandboxed environment) and 33.3% for GPT-5.

In October 2026, CyberChainBench was released, analyzing 541 exploit events across 9 Ethereum-compatible blockchains. The best-performing configuration achieved 37.5%, 43.7%, and 23.4% success rates for detection, exploitation, and patching respectively.

In a simulation, the best-performing agent profited $57.4 million from exploits on 200 exploit events that occurred after the cutoff. Some of the reported high-severity issues were evaluated and determined to not be exploitable by OpenZeppelin. Since much of the data is trained on in the public, results may be exaggerated.

In a recent development, agents will continue to improve, and while current results are not an indication that AI-driven agents are responsible for large scale on-chain thefts, it is an indication that AI can find and exploit weaknesses in smart contracts given a certain environment. Given the ease with which agents can try attacking many different protocols, smaller protocols may see an uptick in exploit attempts.

Teams that implement rigorous testing and monitoring could have an edge over other teams. For example, AI could be used to test a contract prior to deployment, generate regression tests, and identify weird behavior on-chain. A human would still need to verify any potential issues and sign off on changes.

Teams should continue to perform third-party audits and implement other security best practices such as limiting access to sensitive information, setting up alerts and response intends, restricting the amount of money in a wallet, making sure AI systems do not have permissions to transact without human oversight where necessary, and so on.

In a recent development, shiba Inu’s (SHIB) meme currency just got critical acclaim in major United States Perpetuals markets. Nadex, short for North American Derivatives Exchange, filed a motion to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), pursuing time-capped price events.

Industry observers note that conducting business as Crypto.com Derivatives North America, the exchange self-certified a Shiba Inu Strike Event Contract under Commodity Futures Trading Commission regulations. This now allows traditional Derivatives market players exposure to cash-settled event bids.

Recent findings suggest that these SHIB price-tracking contracts do not use traditional margin leverage. They are fully prepaid or collateralized, so the maximum loss per contract is limited to the price paid to enter (plus fees). There is no margin call or unlimited downside in the style of Perpetual Futures.

Recent findings suggest that by this strategy, Shiba Inu’s been placed within an honorable roster of major-cap altcoins. The exchange also submitted strike event contract notices covering blue-chips like XRP, Solana, Stellar (XLM), Dogecoin (DOGE), Litecoin (LTC), Hedera (HBAR), Ondo & Polkadot (DOT).

The fresh Shiba Inu (SHIB) price-linked product is a binary-style swap that lets traders take a position on whether SHIB’s benchmark price finishes above a chosen strike at time expiration. Contracts are eligible for listing since November 13, 2026. Will that lift SHIB’s sloppy volumes?

The popular Japanese guard dog-encrusted meme currency saw a tremendous drop in Spot and Futures markets during Q3 of 2026, pushing the meme coin to dwell at fresh yearly lows. With the Derivatives markets piquing their interest in SHIB, a multi-billion influx could come.

According to recent reports, right now, the trading volumes present a grimy picture of $44.56 million in daily Spot trading volume. This puts Shiba Inu at the sixth position in the meme coin category, ranked by 24-hour trading volume. The canine coin’s down 24% in 30 days, while parent chain ETH slid by 25%.

Further on, the 24-hour turnover rate stood below 2%. On Spot markets, turnover counts SHIB trades already completed, while depth describes orders displayed at the moment of the reading. The same capital can trade repeatedly during a day. Low volumes resemble vague demand.

In a recent development, next up is the major demand retest: if Shiba Inu’s (SHIB) $0.00000353 support bubble holds, the next checkpoint revolves around $0.00000515, with the mid-range extending to $0.000006. Traders need to stay alarmed due to the Parabolic Stop & Reverse (SAR) flashing a ‘sell’ signal on the one-day price charts: bottom may not be in yet.

The $0.00000384 is the level to watch.

In a recent development, meanwhile, key data on Perpetual markets showcase a gradually rising total Open Interest (OI), as leveraged players increase their positions before a presumed drastic price swing. The soft volume hikes haven’t flipped the switch back to bullish.

Long price plays still account for most of liquidations, soaking up $79.81K out of $87.20K in liquidations on SHIB’s regular smart contract.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scammers recently used a fake video of Elon Musk to get people to send them crypto.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scammers recently used a fake video of Elon Musk to get people to send them crypto. It didn’t go to initiative.

Especially since according to Coinbase, it blocked a big chunk of those transfers before the money could disappear.

… and Coinbase stopped $4.7 million from reaching scammers.

It has been revealed that someone put out a YouTube livestream made to look like a Tesla flying car demo. On screen was an AI-made Elon Musk, and the pitch was to send crypto and get 2x back.

More than half a million people tuned in. The stream flashed wallet addresses and QR codes. So, sending money took just a scan.

Industry observers note that in a blog post, Coinbase laid out what happened. In about two hours, hundreds of its customers tried to send funds to the scammers. Its automated fraud system caught about 91% of that.

The real Musk had nothing to do with any of it.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that Coinbase hasn’t mentioned how much of the remaining 9% actually got through.

Its fraud agent watches outgoing transfers as they happen.

If any transfer looks off or iffy, like a payment to a freshly created wallet or something tied to a “giveaway,” the agent in question steps in. In such a case, the agent opens a chat with the user, explains why the transfer might be risky, and prompts them to think twice before proceeding.

Recent findings suggest that it even checks its own replies before showing them. According to Coinbase, no person was involved at any point. Nobody’s account got hacked either. No passwords leaked. People (some of them long-time owners) chose to hit send because the fake Musk was convincing.

Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent.

That is exactly what makes these scams tough.

Industry observers note that it isn’t the first fake Elon Musk either. A doctored video in 2023 reportedly cost victims around $160K. In June 2024, deepfake giveaways popped up on more than 35 YouTube channels during a Starship launch.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data.
  • XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median.
  • It has been revealed that XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data. The options market indicates that traders are now preparing for price swings that could be nearly double XRP's historical seven-day price move.

XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median. This figure far exceeds similar metrics for major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and Solana (SOL).

It has been revealed that XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility. Solana highlights the lowest premium among these four cryptocurrencies, Coinbase remarked.

In a recent development, as the chart below indicates, the options-implied seven-day price move for XRP is around 9.6%, according to Glassnode and Coinbase data as of Nov. 17. This compares to its historical median absolute price move of about 4.9%.

Basically, this means that the options market is signaling a price swing nearly twice as large as XRP's typical seven-day price movement.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, Solana's implied price move is also close to 9.5%, almost the same as XRP's. Yet its historical median weekly price move is much higher at about 6.5%.

The key here is that although both cryptocurrencies exhibit similarly large potential price moves, the magnitude of the expected volatility surprise is significantly greater for XRP relative to its usual trading range.

It has been revealed that for comparison, Bitcoin highlights an options-implied seven-day move of about 6%, versus its historical median of about 3.5%. For Ethereum, these numbers are about 8% and 5.1%, respectively.

Obviously, this latest figure doesn't necessarily imply that XRP is going to crash. It's a sign that options traders expect a big price move regardless of its direction.

Implied volatility is a forward-looking measure. It's based on options prices. The higher the implied volatility, the more traders pay for exposure to potential price movements or protection against them.

Sources indicate that the chart from Coinbase is based on a one-standard-deviation estimate. It's derived by converting annualized at-the-money implied volatility into a seven-day timeframe.

For XRP, the roughly 9.6% implied move represents a statistical range. It's not a guaranteed price target. A one-standard-deviation range suggests about a 68% chance of the price staying within this range under typical modeling assumptions.

Thus, the latest figure of 1.94x implies that XRP's volatility premium remains high despite a slight decrease from the previous reading.

From XRP traders' perspective, this can be a very challenging market environment. For traders using leverage, there could be a high risk of liquidation due to potentially sharp price moves.

Jenna Dewan Faced Criticism, a Partner Suspension, and a Shock Dancing with the Stars Exit. She’s Still Proud.

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that dancing with the Stars fans let out a collective gasp Tuesday night.
  • “I had a great time, and I loved getting to share that with the world,” she stated, moments after being eliminated.
  • Not even 48 hours later, Jenna sat down with Women’s Health to share her story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that dancing with the Stars fans let out a collective gasp Tuesday night. Jenna Dewan and her partner, Val Chmerkovskiy, had earned one of the night’s top scores: 28 out of 30. They also won their dance-off against Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik, tying for second on the leaderboard with Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov. Then host Alfonso Ribeiro called Dewan’s name, eliminating her from competition.

“I had a great time, and I loved getting to share that with the world,” she stated, moments after being eliminated. “All love.”.

Not even 48 hours later, Jenna sat down with Women’s Health to share her story.

Jenna Dewan: Overall, it’s really been the saying, “Two things can be true at once.” There's so many different emotions, and it's kind of hard to even put into words because obviously doing a show like this is such an enormous undertaking, and it's physically, emotionally, mentally, spiritually intense. And so, when that's just finished, it's like a light switch goes off, and then you almost don't even know where you are.

I feel all kinds of things. I feel mostly proud. I feel really proud of myself, and I feel proud of the last dance we gave on the ballroom floor, and I feel obviously sad that it's over, that I don't get to give any more dances out there and create any more special pieces. So I think it's really both. I feel really proud of us, and I feel fulfilled, and I feel filled up, and I also feel sad that the journey of creating dances is over.

According to recent reports, JD: When you are going through the show, it feels like any week could be you. The show is not necessarily a show about dance. It's not necessarily a competition about the best dancer. It's not about the best dance you give. It's so many other elements that go into it, which is great on a reality show front-end. It makes people tune in for all different kinds of reasons, but in doing that, you never know how it's going to go.

Industry observers note that once it started whittling down, it was the two of us. You kind of come to a place of like, “Okay, this could be our moment.” And I had a feeling—it was a tough week as far as some of the online noise, I would say, that goes with doing the show. So it definitely wasn't out of my mind that it could be a possibility.

Recent findings suggest that even before Jenna stepped onto the DWTS dance floor, viewers debated whether she belonged in the competition. How much prior dance experience a celebrity contestant can have—while still being considered a fair competitor—has long been a point of debate among viewers.

Sources indicate that jenna started her career as a dancer, where she toured alongside legendary performers, including Janet Jackson (she appeared in two music videos of the singer’s). In 2006, she landed her breakout role in Step Up, in which she played a classically trained ballerina. She was the host for television indicates World of Dance and Flirty Dancing as well as a judge on Come Dance with Me. Many fans of DWTS cited Jenna’s impressive resume as an unfair advantage. “How is Jenna Dewan part of this? She was a professional dancer. Hello! So unfair already,” one X user wrote on the platform after the official season 35 cast announcement.

Sources indicate that it should be noted, however, Jenna is not the first celebrity to join the show with previous dance experience—and it’s safe to say she’ll be far from the last. Stars like Heather Morris, Jordan Fisher, and Charli D’Amelio have all undergone criticism for joining the show in the past, despite having a substantial leg up among fellow contestants. Even Alfonso, the show’s current host and season 19 winner, had prior dance experience.

JD: I will say, through the history of watching the show and what I know about the show, is I've seen there be an issue with people with dance backgrounds, and that obviously there's a lot of opinions on whether we should even have people compete on the show that have dance backgrounds.

Recent findings suggest that I definitely asked quite a few times, “Are you sure you guys want me on the show?” But the incredible people who do the show were really confident in expressing to me that this show had changed a lot, and that it’s not Dancing with the Stars Who Have Never Danced. They wanted a very dynamic cast with all different levels and strengths they bring to the ballroom. I knew it would be an uphill battle for me for sure, just from the patterns of the show and the loyalists of the show and how they feel. But ultimately, the gift of doing something just for myself was really intoxicating, and it won over any sort of doubts or hesitations I had.

In a recent development, JD: The hardest part of the show, I would say, is it really teaches you that joy and difficulty can exist together. There were so many highs of this journey, and then so many moments of frustration and negative noise and criticism that is honestly sad, because it tries to suck out the joy from the experience.

Even for myself with a dance background, it is vulnerable to put yourself out there in the ballroom every Tuesday and be like, “Hey guys, watch my dance and tell me what you think.” And then you have the whole other element of this social, online, noisy world that is almost like they're looking to tear people down, and I felt that that was an unfortunate shade to this show that didn't need to happen.

In a recent development, JD: Part of the journey of the show is interesting because for the first good couple weeks, you rarely see any of the other contestants, because you are really in your own rehearsal space, and you're just trying to get the dances down as fast as you can with your partner. I think it was rare seeing people in the hallways and connecting with some of the contestants. But yeah, we definitely would talk.

Sources indicate that I think at one point Connor [Wood] made me laugh so hard because he noted he had seen some of the online social negativity, and he said, “Everyone needs to go back to journaling.” I laughed so hard, because he is exactly right. At some point, we all thought it was okay to just get online and to be mean for no reason. We are real human beings that see this and feel this, and I think that that gets forgotten.

When we did the team dance, that was when we really were able to start bonding as the contestants, because we were finally together working towards one dance and in a room together. I absolutely love them, and we were all definitely talking about this and sharing our experiences with this, and how most of us at that point, I think, had taken it off our phone or turned off social media.

JD: Naturally, because of my dance background, there were really high expectations that I put on myself, and that the world was putting on me. I didn't even realize it was happening, but it was creating this feeling that I needed to let go of perfection and kind of just get comfortable being seen and just being there. I didn't need to prove anything.

I think I just realized how much of my life I spent wanting to get things right. And this experience really challenged me in that way, because what I realized is, you just can't grow if you're constantly worried about being perfect. I had to learn to be a little uncomfortable, to be critiqued again, to make some mistakes, to be vulnerable, and just let people see me in the middle of figuring something out. There's actually a lot of freedom in that, because I didn't have ballroom dance down perfectly by the time I got out there.

Industry observers note that JD: I thought that every dance we did. I thought that during the week two jive, and it was intriguing to me that [the judges] were so critical of certain dances. However, when I look back, there was a lot of growth for me.

There was a whole element of this that was sort of discovering my strength in a new way because I have had three children, I've navigated huge life transitions, I've built a career, a family, a life, And now, I'm stepping into this show where I'm pushing myself physically, emotionally, creatively in a way that I haven't in years. So I think I just surprised myself with how strong I am, and not just physically, but emotionally.

Jenna also faced an unexpected complication when her partner, Val, was suspended for one episode of the show following a social media post he made about DWTS judge Carrie Ann Inaba. After Carrie Ann criticized his wife, fellow pro dancer Jenna Johnson, for including what she considered an illegal lift in her routine with Harry Shum Jr., Val posted, “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night.” The now-deleted post was widely interpreted as a reference to the 2022 Academy Awards, when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock after making a joke about his wife, Jada Pinkett Smith.

Industry observers note that carrie Ann appeared to interpret the post as a threat. She shared a screenshot of a Page Six story about it on Instagram, writing, “So this is what we are doing now?”.

On Oct. 17, DWTS production company BBC Studios remarked Val would not participate in the Oct. 20 episode. Jenna danced with pro Alan Bersten in his place.

JD: I said this, and I really mean this, that I did not foresee having as many challenges as I did that were thrown at me during my Dancing with the Stars journey. However, the challenges of it gave me an opportunity to walk my talk, and I always think that when that happens, you can go back to your true north, to what’s your intention for doing something. How do you want to show up as a human when you’re experiencing challenges? And I kept going back to my kids. When the mid-season suspension happened, and all these things were going on, I thought, “I have a real opportunity here. I can be annoyed and bitter and upset about this, or I can show up with grace and love and joy and focus on the moment.”.

That particular week was about my mom and my dedication to her. And she was in town, thrilled to have this dance with me, and thrilled to experience this moment. And I thought that this is something she's going to remember. We're all going to remember my family forever. Let's focus on that, and let's not worry about all of this that's going on.

It has been revealed that JD: I’ve seen that, and I feel like with just life in general, even outside of Dancing with the Stars, that is absolutely something that most females have experienced. I think there's been a great change in our world, but I think for years upon years upon years, women have had a fight against misogyny and inherent bias. Women at times in life are just held to a different standard than men, and I think that that is a real reflection.

We're expected to be exceptional, but also humble and confident, but not too confident, skilled, but not struggling enough to earn praise. There's all this pressure on women. It feels like sometimes if a woman is strong or capable, the expectations become that much higher. I think people are so busy expecting women to be extraordinary that we forget to celebrate them for being extraordinary.

In a recent development, JD: It's never too late for a upcoming chapter in life. And I think if there was like, one thing I wanted people to take away from my whole journey, it’s that we're never finished becoming who we are, and it's never too late to choose your own passion in life and your own joy in life. There isn't some age where you stop growing and dreaming and trying new things.

Recent findings suggest that alyssa Cruz is the social media editor at Women’s Health, where she drives social strategy and helps shape the brand’s voice across platforms. Prior to WH, she worked at CBS News and palabra. Originally from Toledo, she is a proud alumna of Ohio University, where she received two bachelor’s degrees in journalism and Spanish. When she is not creating social content, you can find her trying different restaurants in New York City or planning her next trip.

Home » Blitz news » Anthropic’s Record $81B IPO Is Here—Will It Test Crypto?

The Claude maker priced shares at $83 for a $1.5 trillion valuation as Bitcoin dips 1.5% ahead of Nasdaq trading.

Anthropic has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share, raising roughly $81.3 billion in the largest public market debut in history—just as digital asset markets pull back and traders weigh whether the historic AI listing will siphon retail and institutional liquidity away from crypto.

According to Anthropic’s official announcement, the Claude AI developer priced its shares roughly 6.4% above its previously marketed range of $70 to $78, assigning the company a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion. Trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT is set to begin Thursday, November 19.

While Wall Street absorbed the massive tech offering, the broader cryptocurrency market traded lower on Thursday morning.

In a recent development, total crypto market capitalization dropped 1.3% over the past 24 hours to $2.253 trillion, with Bitcoin (BTC) falling 1.5%, the most among the other top 10 biggest cryptos. Bitcoin is currently trading at $63,585.

Anthropic has expanded its IPO to 980 million shares, up from the initially planned 825 million, following exceptionally strong demand from institutional and retail investors.

Priced at $83 per share, the public offering is expected to raise approximately $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion base offering in June and setting a fresh record.

Sources indicate that the company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement of non-voting shares, priced at the same $83 per share. Reported strategic investors include Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC. Combined, the public offering and private placement are expected to generate more than $107 billion.

Retail investors have been allocated up to 20% of the public offering, representing approximately $16.2 billion. Demand has been particularly strong, with total orders reportedly reaching nearly seven times the number of shares available, according to CNBC.

The deal values Anthropic at approximately $1.5 trillion, marking a dramatic increase from its $965 billion private valuation when it confidentially filed for an IPO in June.

Anthropic’s IPO could have implications for crypto markets beyond the AI sector. The $155 billion in combined IPO capital raised by SpaceX and Anthropic within five months highlights growing competition for institutional liquidity, potentially diverting funds from risk assets such as Bitcoin and altcoins.

The listing also gives retail investors a direct way to bet on AI, potentially reducing demand for crypto-native AI tokens that have attracted investors seeking similar exposure.

It has been revealed that ANT’s market debut will also be closely watched as a gauge of risk appetite. A strong opening could lift sentiment across speculative assets, while a weak performance could reinforce risk-off sentiment in both equities and crypto.

Bitcoin is facing increased fear and panic among traders as its price volatility continues to intensify, causing both retail and institutional investors to move with caution.

While Bitcoin is still struggling to regain momentum amid the persistent market downturn, the latest on-chain data from CryptoQuant reveals that Bitcoin's demand has dropped to its weakest level in 2026.

The data shows that Bitcoin's apparent demand is rapidly showing signs of weakness, with the metric dropping below -290,000 BTC before seeing a brief recovery to about -255,000 BTC as of November 18.

However, this does not provide any relief, as Bitcoin’s apparent demand remains substantially below its monthly average of around -172,000 BTC.

In a recent development, as such, it appears that investors’ interest in accumulating Bitcoin remains significantly subdued by the fear of potential losses. Hence, investors are growing increasingly cautious about entering the market amid the rising selling pressure.

The data reveals that investors are growing increasingly wary of their Bitcoin positions amid growing uncertainty about its potential price movements, as Bitcoin’s price downturn has only intensified over the past few days.

While the asset’s price has dipped further, Bitcoin has suddenly retested $62,000 as of November 18, a price level last seen during the severe price crash in July.

Nonetheless, further data shows that it has briefly recovered to $63,817.43 as of the time of writing, showing a decline of about 1.12% over the past 24 hours.

Despite Bitcoin’s extremely negative demand and weak price movements, market analysts are still positive about a potential reversal, describing the moment as an opportunity to buy at a lower price.

It has been previously observed that while many investors are becoming increasingly bearish, periods of widespread fear can sometimes flush out weaker hands, thereby triggering a change in market direction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dogecoin [DOGE] has been more bark than bite lately.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it down to a newly introduced yearly low on the charts and unfortunately, it doesn’t look like it’ll get back up anytime soon.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, Dogecoin was valued at $0.058. This followed a 3.3% dip over the day.

According to recent reports, things really fell apart on 14th November. DOGE fell from $0.065 to $0.057 in a single day. It also briefly hit $0.055, the lowest level of 2026. DOGE’s volume jumped too, implying that too many were selling at once.

Now, while it managed a small bounce to about $0.060 later, it wasn’t able to hold on to that level.

For context, DOGE was above $0.10 in late September. That’s 44% gone… in less than two months.

The RSI was at 28.9, hinting at oversold conditions. It even sank close to 18 during the crash. The MACD was still deep in the red, though the bars were shrinking just a tad.

Simply put, while the sellers seemed to be worn out, buyers are yet to show up.

Finally, leverage has been draining out too, with Open Interest sliding from about $475 million on the 11th to $362.5 at press time.

That’s a quarter of it gone in a week!

Industry observers note that it is a nervous state of things, and one look at the funding rates will tell you why. It was red during the crash of the 14th, flipped a couple more times, and at press time was back to 0.0052%.

According to recent reports, some traders may be betting on a bounce again, but not in massive numbers. Not yet.

ETFs have been even quieter. According to data from SoSoValue, Spot DOGE ETFs haven’t seen a single day of inflows or outflows since mid-October. A whole month of nothing.

Industry observers note that their total net assets still dropped though. We went from $17 million in late September to about $9.74 million at the time of writing. In simple words, Dogecoin’s falling price has been shrinking what’s already there.

17 Years Ago, Satoshi Nakamoto Opens His BitcoinTalk Account: What Happened Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.
  • According to recent reports, the network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers.
  • In 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

According to recent reports, the network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed consumers on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

In 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and announced their farewell.

The 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an matter we haven't solved 17 years later.

2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of newly introduced technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

However, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

In a recent development, 2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, issues with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

In 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

The next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default.

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, newly introduced research reveals.

A upcoming report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical users into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue users, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Public GitHub activity shows a clear change in focus. New repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

Among AI people, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot launches rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:.

In a recent development, in Bitrue’s survey of users who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Industry observers note that willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents noted they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

According to recent reports, among non-consumers, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot stated they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

Customers who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:.

Sources indicate that AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

The numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

Options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI.

Sources indicate that this suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

Recent findings suggest that according to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

Recent findings suggest that at the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history notes more than its current price action does.

XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

According to recent reports, in the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

On Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

Recent findings suggest that according to the entry, the company claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator said.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure users with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

On the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's fresh crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

On Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he remarked.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CoinShares has revealed that in October, it sold its entire Ethereum [ETH] treasury position and half of its Solana [SOL] holdings.

Industry observers note that the reason? To buy back its own shares.

Housekeeping’s in session at CoinShares!

Industry observers note that the European digital asset manager’s ETH sale brought in $16.6 million, and its SOL sale added another $2.7 million. That’s $19.3 million put together, and none of it is going back to crypto.

Instead, CoinShares is using it to buy back its own stock.

On the 22nd of October, the board cleared up to $40 million for buybacks. This one sale covers close to half of that budget.

The company shared the details in its Q3 results this week. CEO Jean-Maria Mognetti described the sale as a way to keep cash on hand, so CoinShares can step in and buy when the moment is right.

…nearly half of the $40 million authorized by the Board and gives us the flexibility to act when conditions allow.

There is money, but with an asterik.

Revenue at $27.7 million is about 45% lower than a year ago. What rescued the quarter was the manufacturer’s own crypto. Holdings gained $14.4 million in value; it was a nice turnaround from the $5.4 million hit it took in Q2.

According to recent reports, however, there were some bright spots. Lending and trading picked up, so capital markets income went up to $17.8 million. That’s nearly 4x the previous quarter! Operating income also bounced back after a loss in Q2.

Sources indicate that zooming out, though, makes things appear weaker. EBITDA fell 61.4% YoY to $20.6 million. Notably, net income for the first nine months was $15.6 million, compared with $108.8 million at this point last year.

Money kept coming in, even if fees didn’t show it.

In a recent development, coinShares’ investment products had inflows worth $125 million in Q3. Management fees stayed flat at $19.1 million, since crypto prices were sluggish until late September.

They launched a Bitcoin mining ETF for European institutions in July and bought Quant Manager Bastion in September.

December’s the next big step, though. CoinShares is set to join nine Russell indices, including the Russell 2000. Funds worth about $789.9 billion track these indices. If confirmed, the change takes effect after markets close on the 11th of December.

Upcoming research from Grayscale indicates Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.

The catch? Bitcoin’s calmer day-to-day trading hides a massive trap for anyone trying to time dips: almost all of its multi-year gains still come from just a handful of explosive trading days.

In a recent development, in its report, “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Cryptocurrency Risks,” US digital asset manager Grayscale says Bitcoin’s long-term performance is heavily influenced by a handful of trading days. Its returns have “fat tails,” meaning sharp gains and losses occur more frequently than in traditional stocks.

Over the past three years, Bitcoin delivered an annualized return of roughly 60%. Excluding its 10 best days would have cut that figure to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would have raised it to 197%.

The report also notes that Bitcoin has historically rebounded sharply after major declines. Since 2011, it has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50%, although Grayscale notes these declines are not unusually severe compared with stocks and bonds when adjusted for volatility.

Grayscale also sees Bitcoin as a potential portfolio diversifier because it is less exposed to traditional market factors.

In a recent development, the company points out that Bitcoin has historically recovered sharply after significant declines. Since 2011, Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns of more than 50% from previous highs.

Recent findings suggest that the report cites Bitcoin’s inclusion in J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions as a milestone.

Grayscale describes JPMorgan as a $5 trillion investment manager that now examines Bitcoin alongside established asset classes.

The banks’ 10-year base case for Bitcoin projects a 10% compound annualized return for Bitcoin over the next decade, the highest among the asset classes covered. The forecast also assumes 55% annualized volatility and a 33% correlation with US large-cap stocks, the number below international equities, corporate bonds and hedge funds.

In Bitcoin’s early years, volatility routinely exceeded 100% and at times approached 200%, with a market cap in the single-digit billions.

Grayscale ties the decline to roughly 43% to larger market value and liquidity, greater institutional participation, Bitcoin exchange-traded products and regulatory clarity.

In historical tests, modest Bitcoin allocations raised annualized return and Sharpe ratio in a representative institutional portfolio.

Over three years, Bitcoin explained about half of return variation across FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over the past two years, while Bitcoin led none.

Sources indicate that JPMorgan’s decision to include Bitcoin in its long-term forecasts, along with declining volatility, could shape how institutions approach crypto investments. At the same time, Grayscale’s data indicates how much Bitcoin’s long-term performance depends on a small number of trading days, highlighting the risks of trying to time the market.

Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Recent findings suggest that four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that users will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

In a recent development, binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Owners are strongly advised to patch and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

In related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in users’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

A Brooklyn Townhouse Celebrates a Forgotten Design Pioneer
