📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in the early 1920s, the Pittsburgh-based manufacturer Armstrong Cork Company (now Armstrong World Industries) made the prescient move of tapping a young arts educator named Hazel Dell Brown to act as its in-house decorator. Hers would be an under-recognized yet wildly influential career. Over the course of more than three decades, she designed countless rooms for advertisements, booklets, catalogs, and more that showcased the brand’s products, chief among them linoleum flooring. With their bold colors, fearless mix of patterns, and daring pastiche, her interiors shaped an entire generation of homes in the Rust Belt and beyond.

According to recent reports, for two contemporary artists setting out to renovate a Brooklyn town house for their young family, Brown’s little-known work recently served not only as inspiration but also as a litmus test. When interviewing architects to take on the project, the couple first presented examples of vintage Armstrong schemes. “A lot of people would take one look and then show me something different,” reflects the wife, who learned about Brown while working on a project in Pittsburgh. Not so in the case of Tal Schori and Rustam Mehta of GRT Architects. The AD100 duo instantly responded to Brown’s surface-heavy approach and inward-facing embrace of small spaces, or as Schori puts it, “rooms within rooms.” As for their interior designer, Penelope August, a friend of the wife’s since preschool—she implicitly passed with flying colors.

A circa 1980 Gio Ponti chandelier crowns the living room, which is furnished with a vintage Vladimir Kagan sectional sofa and a Jens Risom chair upholstered in a custom fabric based on a Macgregor Harp painting; artwork by Rose Marcus and wallpaper by Antoinette Poisson.

The kitchen features art-glass cabinet fronts by Paul Wissmach Glass Manufacturer and a custom terrazzo floor inspired by ancient roman mosaics of unswept debris.

The attic’s custom oak millwork.

Hembus wallpaper in a custom blue distinguishes the primary bedroom; painting (above bed) by Michael Wang.

Sources indicate that the project evolved into a dynamic collaboration as the couple and their team gutted the town house, set in Carroll Gardens and previously renovated in the 1990s. Together they took care to preserve historic details like the original doors and staircase, with its original mahogany newel posts and handrails. Wherever appropriate, they embraced imperfections, filling in the gaps between old floorboards with contrasting tinted epoxy and leaving levels ever so askew. “This house shows signs of age and that’s not a bad thing,” states Schori. Adds Mehta, “As artists, they understood what is and isn’t precious so that the home does not feel overly restored.”.

The backyard was updated by Brook Landscape, with a shed and swing set by GRT Architects.

In the son’s room, shaker-style cabinetry reveals a reading nook.

A refurbished tub from The Demolition Depot anchors the primary bath, which is lined in tiles by Balineum (on walls) and Artistic Tile (on floor).

It has been revealed that brown was nothing if not a gleeful problem solver, presenting flexible solutions to the needs of everyday life, often through inventive secondary spaces. (“Your rumpus room can be anything you like” proclaimed one Armstong campaign.) True to that strategy, GRT devised a floor blueprint full of versatile surprises. Adjoining the dining room is a cave-like lounge for watching television or just relaxing, with a pass-through to the kitchen for the easy arrival of snacks. Opposite the cookspace—more on that showstopper later—is a cozy breakfast area, with a load-bearing skylight that offers glimpses of the roof terrace (and sometimes curious children) above. And on the second level, a secret passage leads from the primary suite into the library, one column of shelving concealing a door. “All these appendages to the main spaces allow multiple things to happen at once,” says Schori.

In the daughter’s room, Shaker-style trim is painted in Farrow & Ball’s Blue Ground.

The kids’ bath mixes terrazzo walls with custom floor tiles by Haand.

Oak millwork incorporates vintage Piero Fornasetti panels in the dining room, where Guillerme et Chambron chairs surround an antique farm table; painting by Jo Nigoghossian, and custom fireplace fabricated by Daniel Armitano.

In a recent development, surfaces and furnishings tend toward the eclectic and one-of-a-kind, with a mix of wallpapers and fabrics, some deadstock, setting the stage for vintage treasures. In the living room, a Vladimir Kagan sectional sofa found at auction doubles as a jungle gym of sorts. The primary bath is anchored by a salvaged earthenware tub, since glazed a light blue to complement the retro checkerboard tiles and scalloped vanity. And the dining room’s custom millwork incorporates a series of midcentury Fornasetti panels. Doorknobs, lighting, motifs, art by their circle of creative friends—it’s all a mishmash. “We liked things independently of how they worked together,” claims the wife. Adds August: “It was so fun to stitch all these elements into an old house—I love a space where you come upon something unexpected.”.

A detail of the kitchen’s terrazzo floor indicates stone and metal shapes (some abstract, some legible) inspired by detritus.

A custom sofa frames the lounge off the dining room, which has a pass-through to the kitchen; carpet by Stark.

In the living room, a Gretta Johnson painting hangs above the fireplace, which is flanked by artworks by Cletus Johnson (left) and Ted Mineo (near right) and Miles Huston (Far right).

The husband’s office/music room is cocooned in cork; painting (at left, bottom) by MacGregor Harp.

The stairwell’s painted checkerboard floor hints at classic Americana.

Industry observers note that floor to floor, the mood shifts. The son’s and daughter’s rooms each riff on classic Shaker woodwork, with rails and built-in cabinetry that respond to the exposed ceiling joists. Enlivened by a splatter-painted floor and celestial configuration of ceiling lights, the plywood-lined attic operates as a kids’ club, craft room, and family theater in one. (How’s that for a rumpus room, Hazel?) Thanks to some clever excavation and engineering on the part of GRT, the combined garden level and cellar is now a double-height studio for the wife, complete with a gantry crane for hoisting heavy sculptures. Outside, meanwhile, Brook Landscape transformed the backyard into a romantic swath of greenery.

Vintage globe lights from a one-time optometry office add a surreal touch to the powder room.

Loose arrangements of greenery frame the steps to the backyard.

GRT Architects combined the garden level and cellar into a double-height art studio with a register of exposed brick.

A vintage Vilhelm Lauritzen ceiling light punctuates the primary bedroom; painting by Margaux Ogden.

As for that kitchen, here the team took inspiration not only from Brown but from two additional touchstones. Cabinet fronts nod to art glass at the Upper East Side’s late great Glaser’s Bake Shop, the salvaged interiors of which August and the wife chanced upon at The Demolition Depot. The floor, meanwhile, riffs on ancient Roman mosaics of unswept detritus, an example of which can be found at the Vatican Museums. “We wanted a kitchen that wouldn’t look bad if it got messy,” says the wife. Working closely with GRT and August, she and her husband evolved that historic precedent into a contemporary series of shapes, some abstract and some legible (a knife, a carrot, a wine glass). Rendered in scraps of stone or metal, their forms now appear to float in poured terrazzo.

“The way artists think about objects and architecture is as a constant work in progress,” says Mehta. “These are visual people with an incredible mental library of references.” Would Brown approve? Without a doubt. As the designer once wrote: “Whatever you do, use your own ideas. Don’t be afraid of them.”.

  • In the first quarter of 2026, RBC reported buying shares of the spot Bitwise XRP ETF for about $30,000.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, royal Bank of Canada (RBC) held no shares of the Teucrium 2x Long Daily XRP ETF at the end of the second quarter, according to an amended Form 13F that the bank filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Nov. 18, 2026. The Teucrium fund gives investors double leveraged exposure to XRP.

In the first quarter of 2026, RBC reported buying shares of the spot Bitwise XRP ETF for about $30,000. XRP was trading at $0.99 on Thursday.

Sources indicate that the latest wave of 13F filings came out in November and covers the third quarter through Sept. 30. Goldman Sachs held about $144 million in XRP ETFs at the end of the third quarter, up from about $87 million at the end of the second quarter, according to its filing. The bank held shares of five spot funds from Franklin Templeton, Bitwise, Canary, Grayscale and 21Shares, and its crypto portfolio was worth $2.64 billion.

In a recent development, italy's Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed XRP fund holdings of $27.21 million. The bank held 712,319 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF, worth about $20.52 million, and it also opened a fresh position of 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF, worth about $6.7 million. Besides, trading firm Jane Street reported about $23.5 million in XRP funds.

According to recent reports, UBS and Morgan Stanley disclosed XRP fund holdings of $1.91 million and $116,000, respectively. Bank of America held 13,260 shares of the futures-based Volatility Shares XRP ETF, worth about $106,600.

Wells Fargo held about $11,000 in the Bitwise fund, and JPMorgan Chase held 539 shares of the same fund, worth about $9,000. National Bank of Canada held 330 shares of the Bitwise fund, worth about $5,500, and Bank of Montreal held REX-Osprey and ProShares Ultra XRP shares worth $4,300.

Industry observers note that U.S. spot XRP ETFs held $1.08 billion in total assets as of Nov. 17, according to SoSoValue.

It has been revealed that form 13F filings only capture long positions in US-listed securities on a specific date. They don't show shorts, derivative hedges, intra-quarter trading or assets held outside the United States.

  • XRP could rebound toward $1.06–$1.07 as tentative signs of a bottom emerge, according to Cilinix.
  • Recent findings suggest that XRP may have room to recover toward $1.06 and $1.07, according to the host of Cilinix Crypto, whose latest XRP analysis points to tentative signs of a bottom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Tackles $1.07; Broader Downtrend Still Looms.

XRP could rebound toward $1.06–$1.07 as tentative signs of a bottom emerge, according to Cilinix.

Recent findings suggest that XRP may have room to recover toward $1.06 and $1.07, according to the host of Cilinix Crypto, whose latest XRP analysis points to tentative signs of a bottom. The forecast is conditional: renewed weakness in equities could instead send the token back toward $0.90 and $0.85.

The distinction matters. The host sees enough improvement to support a short-term rebound, but not enough to call an end to the larger downtrend. “The higher timeframe structure is still very bad,” the analyst remarked.

It has been revealed that the technical argument rests partly on XRP reclaiming its seven-day rolling volume-weighted average price, or VWAP, after a period of declines. The host noted that earlier recoveries above that measure had preceded upward moves, while cautioning that the indicator does not always carry much significance.

XRP had also moved back into the developing monthly value area, with an initially favorable reaction. Together, those developments gave the analyst more confidence that the market could stabilize and gradually push higher.

It has been revealed that there is a weakness in that setup, however. XRP broke above a previous swing high but swiftly fell back below it and had not reclaimed it at the time of the analysis. The host described that part of the structure as “slightly bearish.”.

Funding rates offered another supporting signal. They turned sharply negative around the recent lows before becoming positive again, which the analyst viewed as consistent with a potentially defended bottom, not confirmation of a lasting reversal.

Industry observers note that the broader backdrop kept the host cautious. Oil prices remained low and the volatility index had opened lower, but the S&P 500 was still near its lows.

Cilinix also cited a lack of ETF inflows as one reason not to adopt an XRP outlook that ran against the wider market.

Sources indicate that the $1.06–$1.07 area is therefore a potential recovery zone, not a confirmed breakout target. Cilinix would become more conservative there because of the weak higher-timeframe structure.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ambcrypto ↗ Open Full Page

Bitcoin miner fees hit a 15-year low – Why profit margins are shrinking

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (492 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure.
  • According to Glassnode’s recent update, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.
  • This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure. This, in turn has resulted in miners increasingly selling their Bitcoin reserves instead of holding them for long-term appreciation.

According to Glassnode’s recent update, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.

This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.

At the same time, there is also a decline in transaction fee revenue. With 11 months into 2026, Bitcoin miners earned just 912 BTC in transaction fees, the lowest annual total since at least 2011. This is a huge drop compared to 1,720 BTC in 2025 and 15,178 BTC in 2024.

According to recent reports, in other words, transaction fees accounted for only 0.63% of total miner revenue in 2026, down from 1% in 2025 and 6.5% in 2023. This is enough proof that demand for Bitcoin block space has weakened, reducing the contribution of this revenue source.

Remarking on the same, CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock said,.

Like with any commodity production business, it should get harder and thinner margin over time because the lowest cost operators should be the most successful and durable.

In other words, Sudock believes Bitcoin mining will become increasingly competitive over the next decade, with shrinking profit margins favoring operators with the lowest production and electricity costs.

He expects the global hashrate to continue growing, but at a slower pace than in the previous ten years, as mining hardware becomes more efficient and large publicly listed miners explore AI data centers.

He also argued that Bitcoin mining will not depend solely on large public companies, as smaller businesses and privately held miners can operate profitably.

At the same time, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju noted that Bitcoin’s average mining cost reached approximately $62,862 in Q3 2026, based on Marathon Digital’s filings. With BTC trading near this level, miners are facing shrinking profit margins and could face potential losses if prices fall further.

However, the relatively high hashrate suggests miners remain committed to the network despite growing profitability concerns.

This comes as Bitcoin miners are shifting their focus towards AI and high-performance computing (HPC), as investors increasingly value their power infrastructure and data centers.

Companies such as Core Scientific, IREN, and TeraWulf are generating significant revenue from AI infrastructure and HPC services, in some cases surpassing their Bitcoin mining income.

However, the Miner Outflow chart suggests that compared with the rest of the year, November outflows are calm.

At the same time, the Miner Reserve chart was at about 1.1925 million BTC at press time. In fact, through October and into November, it moved in a narrow band, roughly between 1.192 million and 1.1926 million.

All in all, miners are roughly holding steady, with small accumulation or lower net selling.

XRP Outperforms Solana and Dogecoin in Japan

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.
  • In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the company highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.
  • Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the company highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This shows that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are right now trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data demonstrated Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

37 Best Housewarming Gifts to Get You Welcomed Back (2026)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yes, the best housewarming gifts should ideally be useful, but that doesn’t mean you should completely abandon elements of charm and whimsy when you’re selecting the perfect item.
  • With that in mind, we’ve rounded up the best housewarming gifts—many of which have blessed our own spaces—at various price points.
  • Here are some of our absolute favorite housewarming gift ideas for kicking off a whole latest era of feeling at home, in an elevated way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yes, the best housewarming gifts should ideally be useful, but that doesn’t mean you should completely abandon elements of charm and whimsy when you’re selecting the perfect item. Whether you’re bestowing something special upon a newly introduced homeowner or a pal settling into a new apartment, a vibe-enhancing and aesthetically pleasing present goes a long way to add warmth and personality to any new space.

With that in mind, we’ve rounded up the best housewarming gifts—many of which have blessed our own spaces—at various price points. You’ll find practical presents, such as throw blankets and kitchen tools; home decor items, like chic glassware; and a few indulgences, like caviar. Conveniently, several options also work as hostess gifts.

Here are some of our absolute favorite housewarming gift ideas for kicking off a whole latest era of feeling at home, in an elevated way.

Industry observers note that this lightweight set of borosilicate glasses has a playful raised-spot pattern. They’re blessedly dishwasher-safe, which matters a lot for glasses in daily use.

This high-quality reprint of a 1902 guest book is shopping writer Julia Harrison’s go-to housewarming gift. The book instructs guests to draw a pig rather than the more traditional practice of writing a note. This is “for most guests, a great relief,” indicates Harrison.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not often that we come across a toolbox that is actually attractive. This model from Japanese brand Toyo sure is, and it’s just the right size for essentials, like screwdrivers, a level, and a measuring tape. It’s sure to get used by the end of the first week in every new home.

Kitchen towels get used harder than almost anything else in a new home. These are heavy cotton terry made in Portugal, with a jacquard pattern on one side and loops on the other. They’re thick enough to stand in for a trivet on many surfaces, which most kitchen towels can’t claim.

Gifting someone beautiful custom stationery is a thoughtful and useful way to make their fresh chapter that much more official. It’s one of the easier housewarming gifts to personalize, and you’re sure to smile when you receive a handwritten thank-you note.

It has been revealed that this isn’t your grandpa’s soap on a rope. Ash’s revamp involves a spicy yet floral scent and a pop of color in its elegant red string.

For those who prefer to sip their spirits neat, these hand-blown mezcal glasses are a vibrant way to toast to the new digs.

Do the eternal (or aspirational!) host or hostess a favor, and introduce this AD-favorite coffee table book into their collection. Its pages are full of dinner-party inspiration, including interviews with tastemakers, like Laura Gonzalez, about their entertaining philosophy.

Any coffee enthusiast will treasure a high-quality French press, and we’re partial to this design from Le Creuset. The kitchen must-have is available in a number of colorways to suit neutral tastes or a more maximalist style.

Feed their caffeine addiction with style by showing up to a housewarming with a sleek-looking coffee maker and a bag of their favorite French roast.

It has been revealed that help the amateur chef in your friend group get a head start on their new home’s kitchen essentials. Flamingo Estate is known for its homegrown pantry wares; this oil-and-vinegar gift set includes a California-grown olive oil and persimmon vinegar. In a rush? This gift set comes conveniently prewrapped.

Industry observers note that steak knives don’t feel like an essential until you’re sawing through prime rib with a butter knife. We love this set for its approachable price point and handsome riveted wood handle. (And don’t worry, though inspired by a 19th-century French design, these blades are dishwasher-safe.).

These hand-painted candles elevate the traditional taper. Choose between three floral motifs to best suit their style and personality.

It has been revealed that take the stress out of floral arrangements with a ruffled set of bud vases. Each varies in height to make a dramatic array, whether filled with single stems or small bunches.

It has been revealed that senior shopping editor Nashia Baker loves this blanket, which she claims is “incredibly fluffy, warm, and easy to care for.” The faux mohair throw feels soft, has elegant-looking plush tassels at either end, and it’s light enough to stay out on the sofa all year. It comes in a variety of colorways that will accent and elevate any living room.

In a recent development, anyone with a predilection for kitschy-chic home decor will swoon over these delicate shell napkin rings from Gohar World. Gifting this set will likely seal your invite to their upcoming dinner party.

A bouquet is a classic gift on its own, but you can level it up by presenting it arranged in a stunning vase. This one from Zara Home features a graphic black-and-white stripe that perfectly contrasts a soft floral display.

The best incense holders look like intentional objects even when you’re out of palo santo. Made from raw sand clay, this piece closely mimics the luxurious look of marble while maintaining a playful shape that transforms your tabletop into a micro sculpture garden.

Every kitchen needs a salt dish, and this handcrafted set moves from the counter to the tabletop with ease. Just add a loaf of fresh bread and a good cutting board for the ideal food-prep setup.

Recent findings suggest that if they’ve finally retired their mismatched plates, this is the replacement they need. The 12-piece set from Villeroy & Boch serves four in white porcelain that’s textured to look like matte slate. It would make an equally good wedding gift.

Cheaper napkins exist, of course, but how many resemble 12th-century geometric stone mosaics? This set of four from Cabana will become an heirloom. While hand-embroidered napkins might be a particularly kind touch, purchasing these is perhaps the more sensible choice if you’re on a tight timeline (and don’t know how to stitch).

The hand-blown glass bottle arrives filled with Le Soir hand and body wash, scented with cedar and tangerine. But it will look just as good by the sink once it’s refilled with whatever they buy next.

According to recent reports, A custom caviar tin is the fanciest way to celebrate newly introduced beginnings. This one from CY Kitchen comes with a mother-of-pearl serving spoon to complete the experience.

Recent findings suggest that ensure a new homeowner’s greenery thrives with a shiny new watering can and mister gift set. The sculptural design is great for those who still want to prioritize aesthetics when tending to their plant babies.

Industry observers note that cheese boards are a longstanding go-to housewarming gift, and this oyster platter is a surprising and luxurious take on the dishware. It looks like it was plucked right off Gwyneth Paltrow’s kitchen wall and will definitely get a ton of use from a lover of seafood.

Channel a French café vibe with this elevated cutlery set from Parisian label Sabre.

For your coziest friend, a luxe throw blanket is the gift that keeps on giving—for movie nights, late mornings, and everything in between.

Recent findings suggest that winding stainless steel creates a surrealist botanical motif across the handles of these salad servers. They’re so good, we’re gifting them to everyone we know as housewarming gifts and as a wedding gift when the registry has been picked over.

For the friend who moved solely for a better kitchen, a handblown glass cake stand can almost guarantee that you’ll be the first on call when it’s time to taste-test those new recipes.

For the fashionable host or hostess: This tablecloth takes plissé pleats out of their wardrobe and puts it onto their table.

Little comes in handy as much as a tabletop lighter. Suddenly, there’s no need to rifle through drawers, searching for matches to set the ambience. This sculptural ceramic option looks intentionally placed wherever it sits and makes for a great conversation piece.

It has been revealed that for all the champagne toasts to come, SLJ’s coupe set feels special enough to mark any big occasion or milestone. Most people already move in with a set of wine glasses, making coupes the perfect gift.

Industry observers note that salt cellars have risen in popularity over the last few years, and the designs of these humble culinary staples have only gotten more imaginative. This version from AD100 designer Beata Heuman makes for a cute kitchen companion.

These art deco glasses are the perfect size for a short cocktail, whether a sophisticated pregame sip or a low-alc nightcap. The mini size makes them stand apart from the rest of your glassware.

North Carolina metalsmith Colby Shelton Byrd designed these spiral servers exclusively for East Fork. The stainless steel has real heft, and they’ll toss a salad or serve pasta at the first dinner in the new place.

Recent findings suggest that before thoughtfully gifting this generously sized cushion with a linen-and-cotton canvas front and a linen back, definitely inquire about the color of their sofa. But should you forget, this oceanic blue is an elegant yet unexpected take on a neutral.

What’s Coming for Solana in 2027? Upgrade Planned Across Four Key Areas

  • According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

Industry observers note that the Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

According to recent reports, after Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

It has been revealed that solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

According to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

Recent findings suggest that “So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more promptly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

According to recent reports, “Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

It has been revealed that watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

Danielle Frankel Reimagines the 21st Century Bridal Store

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1284 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that after nearly 10 years in business, fashion designer Danielle Frankel Hirsch has opened a 12,000-square-foot location in Tribeca with interiors set to change the bridal game.
  • The nearly two-year design process is complete, and the Danielle Frankel bridal salon is now ready for appointments.
  • Industry observers note that frankel Hirsch on the staircase wearing a shirt she designed from Fortuny fabric.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after nearly 10 years in business, fashion designer Danielle Frankel Hirsch has opened a 12,000-square-foot location in Tribeca with interiors set to change the bridal game. To create the new space, which opened in early November, Frankel Hirsch worked with AD PRO Directory designer Augusta Hoffman and Studio Partners Architecture.

The nearly two-year design process is complete, and the Danielle Frankel bridal salon is now ready for appointments. “We’re finally at the point where my heart and my head have been,” says Frankel Hirsch, who worked with Hoffman on her previous Los Angeles boutique and Fresh York City atelier. “Because this is our third space together, we can almost speak in shorthand now.”.

Industry observers note that frankel Hirsch on the staircase wearing a shirt she designed from Fortuny fabric. Hoffman used the same Fortuny print throughout the space for wrapping side tables, keepsake boxes on the shelves, as well as for the woven seats on barstools.

The unassuming entrance to Danielle Frankel on Hudson Street.

In the reception room just inside the street entrance, the desk is custom, the chairs are antique, and the custom pendant is by Jamb.

Hoffman worked with the artist Miriam Ellner to create eglomise paneling surrounding the staircase. “The eglomise is one of my favorite things because when we were working with the artist we worked so intimately with her,” Frankel Hirsch notes. “We worked on the placement the way that we do our laces. We kept going back and forth with the drawings because I wanted it to feel like our lace placement.”.

Recent findings suggest that on a recent morning, a bride and her wedding party were busy in the VIP suite making a final selection. The beaming group entered the space through an unassuming brown storefront entrance on Harrison Street, its two large glass windows encased in a sheer linen. From there they ascended a staircase up to a large gallery with over 30-foot floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the streets below on two sides, and a hand-painted mural pattern above on the ceiling.

The interiors of the original 19th-century Queen Anne–style red brick building were transformed by Hoffman (full disclosure: I am writing Hoffman’s design monograph publishing with Rizzoli in Fall 2027) into a modern, elegant bridal boutique that honors the history of the original New York Mercantile Exchange, first established in the 1880s to keep the standards of the grocer business. “We wanted the space to stay pretty bright and focus on the architecture, but we needed a lot of seating,” Hoffman says. “There was a lot of pressure because we wanted it to feel like Danielle and we wanted to leave our mark on the space, but it’s also so beautiful as is and we didn’t want to have too many interventions that take away from that.”.

The rug, vintage Dutch leather armchairs, and custom clothing racks create one of the four seated zones in the gallery area. The wall features antique mottled glass windows. “We wanted this wall to feel historically accurate,” Hoffman notes.

The custom oak screen features shelves for displaying miniature gowns by Danielle Frankel. The shelves are lined in silver leaf. The antique stool is reupholstered in a Fortuny fabric.

In a recent development, the view of the gallery area from a second floor bridal suite. The vintage teak seating set is reupholstered in a fabric by Manuel Canovas and the glass cocktail tables and Fortuny wrapped side tables are custom. The custom window panels are by Augusta Hoffman Studio for Wovn Home and the custom curtain hardware are bronze leaves designed by Hoffman. Hoffman pulled the leaf design from the details on the columns.

What previously functioned as a large, open space with a small mezzanine, had little existing infrastructure–no electrical, HVAC, or plumbing—and is now an area where brides can plot as they make the most important decision for their wedding day. In the gallery, Hoffman created distinct zones where wedding parties wait before their appointment in a private fitting room.

Much of the furniture was sourced by Hoffman and Frankel Hirsch together on trips to Paris. Antique glass vitrines separate the space, which they included from the previous New York gallery and filled with Frankel Hirsch’s own family wedding photos as well as printed details brides can use for their fitting. One vitrine has a board layered with references of crinoline and interlining. Another has custom Danielle Frankel cufflinks. An oak folding screen lines one half of the room, with miniature gowns set on shelves lined in silver leaf paper. Custom parchment and cerused oak racks Hoffman designed to withstand the weight of a wedding dress line the floor displaying roughly 65 dresses from Danielle Frankel collections.

The reflection of the wall is seen in the mirrored structure designed to house the elevator bank and stairwell to the street entrance. A framed antique floral plaster relief is flanked with 1930s Italian wall sconces in patinated glass and metal.

Industry observers note that the staircase and elevator bank within the mirrored structure. “We had to add the elevator for function and for code, and we were like ‘How do we take this existing architecture and put an elevator in the middle of the room?’” Hoffman claims. “It feels super unexpected, versus trying to hide it, and you get to see more of the surrounding architecture and light in the reflection.”.

The custom rug is topped with an antique stool upholstered in a Fortuny fabric, a 1950s chair, and a 19th-century English pine console table.

The view from the sitting area adjacent to a bar. The vintage teak seating set was among the first items Hoffman and Frankel Hirsch sourced for the space. The custom bar stool is woven with a Fortuny fabric.

It has been revealed that the view from within the staircase to the gallery area. The custom center table is by Rafael Carneiro Triboli and the French chairs are from the 1930s.

It has been revealed that hoffman and Studio Partners Architects took what was formerly the mezzanine, originally separated from the below with only a single-bar metal railing, and made it into a full wall with antiqued mottled glass windows. In the center they constructed a cascading grand staircase, cleverly concealing the stockroom underneath, which leads upstairs to three private bridal suites. The hallways, painted in Wenge by Benjamin Moore, lead to the bridal suites, each designed differently and filled with antique and vintage furniture, custom carpets, lighting, and racks. The walls are painted in Presidente Roman Clay by Portola Paints, an earthy contrast to the white and ivory dresses, which are naturally the center of attention for visitors in each room.

When guests are finished in their suites, there’s a bar in the gallery space where wedding parties can sit and make the final selection. The wedding party that morning had selected the dress and were toasting champagne to celebrate. “It’s just as much about the hospitality and the warmth as it is about the gowns,” Frankel Hirsch says.

In the VIP bridal suite, which can be accessed through a discreet entrance on Harrison Street, the custom sofa is upholstered in Holland & Sherry’s Corbel in Henna. The artwork features fragments of 19th century Japanese brocade.

The midcentury armchairs are upholstered in a Watts 1874 fabric and flank a vintage oak table.

The rack, mirror, and ceiling pendant are all custom in the VIP bridal suite.

In the dressing area of the VIP bridal suite, the ceiling pendant is custom and the closet wall covering is by Watts 1874.

The 1930s lounge chair is reupholstered in a Fortuny fabric and the 1970s lamp is from Brazil.

Kia’s PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.
  • The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
  • According to recent reports, A year after it went on sale, the PV5 promptly became Europe’s most popular small electric van.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.

The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.

According to recent reports, A year after it went on sale, the PV5 promptly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.

Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.

It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.

Recent findings suggest that the PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

Industry observers note that that’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.

Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia looks to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.

It has been revealed that it will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia noted the newly introduced PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.

A plena capacidad la nueva #PV7 consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero #Kia #KiaPV7 #MovementThatInspires pic.twitter.com/fzIvviYZuE.

Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.

Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.

According to recent reports, thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.

With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.

According to recent reports, the PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.

Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.

The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.

Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.

The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.

The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.

Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov.
  • Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

K33 Research noted bitcoin is trading in “deep value territory” after a 14% weekly drop, arguing that “any entry below $70K is a gift from the market” for medium- to long-term investors.

The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov. 16. Head of research Vetle Lunde wrote that bitcoin’s slide has erased its August and September gains and left the market deeply oversold. Bitcoin has posted six straight red weekly candles and is on track for a record 13 consecutive days of lower daily highs, according to K33.

Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan. 26 to March 1, 2026, and from April 3 to May 29, 2022. Daily RSI, a momentum gauge, hit 19.95 on Saturday and has stayed below 25 since Friday. Bitcoin also fell below its 200-week moving average, near $68,000, after its worst weekly return since June 7.

Sources indicate that at the bottom on Nov. 15, bitcoin traded about 8.5% under the 200-week average, a wider gap than the 7.3% recorded at June’s low of $58,500. K33 said 51.5% of the bitcoin supply last moved on-chain at prices above the current level, meaning the average holder could have sold for more at some point in the past four years.

Lunde stated those readings, taken together, have typically lined up with market bottoms. K33 also noted that crypto has lagged traditional markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recovering modestly last week while bitcoin sank.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin was trading near $62,300 on Wednesday, according to Coinbase spot prices, below the roughly $65,000 level cited in the K33 report, which showed bitcoin down 14% on the week and about 20% over 30 days. Ether also fell 14% over the week, to around $1,827.

Sources indicate that capital continues to leave bitcoin funds. Net outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded products reached 44,900 BTC over the 14 trading days since Oct. 29, K33 said, short of the record of about 71,000 BTC set in June. Total ETF holdings fell to about 1.46 million BTC, the lowest since Aug. 19, and leveraged ETF exposure dropped to 21,900 BTC, the lowest since March 2024.

Sources indicate that forced selling hit derivatives, too. About $1.3 billion in long positions were liquidated on Nov. 13 and 14 as bitcoin broke below $70,000, K33 stated, and funding rates on perpetual futures repeatedly turned negative. Open interest fell by about 30,000 BTC but stayed above 330,000 BTC, leaving leverage elevated against historical norms.

Industry observers note that institutional futures players largely stayed on the sidelines. Open interest in bitcoin futures on CME stayed below 100,000 BTC all week, K33 said, a sign that regulated-market participants have not rushed in to buy the dip.

Demand for downside protection is also surging. The one-month 25-delta skew, which compares the price of puts to calls, rose above 20 for the first time since July, a level Lunde stated has historically coincided with “selling exhaustion near local bottoms.”.

Stablecoins offer another sign of stress. K33 noted net redemptions totaled $16.1 billion over the past month, the largest outflow since the collapse of Terra.

Lunde stopped short of calling the decline over. He remarked earlier recoveries from similar conditions involved “prolonged consolidation,” pointing to a choppy recovery rather than an immediate rebound.

Sources indicate that there were some constructive signs in trading activity. Spot volume ran near $5 billion a day from Friday through Sunday, the busiest weekend since February, which K33 noted could give the market firmer footing after weeks of one-way selling.

In a recent development, even so, leverage remains high, and ETF money is still heading out the door. Bitcoin was near $62,300 at the time of writing, below the roughly $68,000 200-week average K33 flagged as a key level.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Binance Futures added a perpetual contract tied to BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) on Nov. 18.

The contract (IBITUSDT) gives eligible traders round-the-clock exposure to the Nasdaq-listed fund, settles in Tether’s USDT, and offered up to 20x leverage at launch.

Recent findings suggest that binance set the opening for 09:45 UTC in a listing notice, and the exchange’s public futures ticker recorded trades after the scheduled opening. The contract keeps trading after the fund’s market closes, and Binance’s mark price can still move far enough to trigger liquidation.

Traders can take a position on IBIT's rise or fall without owning its shares or Bitcoin, as the fund seeks to reflect Bitcoin's price.

Binance’s TradFi FAQ lists the UK, Hong Kong, Taiwan and some European Economic Area countries as common examples of restricted markets for these products. The 20x figure is the launch ceiling, and Binance’s margin rules set lower leverage ceilings for larger positions.

The price index is Binance’s reference for the underlying and helps feed the mark price, the estimate the exchange uses to determine whether a position has reached its liquidation threshold.

According to recent reports, during regular equity trading, Binance builds its reference index from third-party price quotes. It smooths those quotes during premarket and after-hours trading, then gives new quotes less weight during the overnight session, according to Binance’s pricing methodology.

On weekends, holidays, and during covered maintenance periods without those quotes, Binance looks to the futures order book, where traders place buy and sell orders for the perpetual.

In a recent development, it averages two measures from that book, the impact bid and impact ask, then smooths the result by giving more weight to recent readings. The index can keep moving while the ETF’s last share price stays where trading left it.

On weekends, holidays and maintenance windows when vendor quotes are unavailable, Binance uses the futures order book to build its index.

The mark can reach a position’s liquidation threshold while the ETF market is closed.

Shows the documented pricing mechanism. Live prices, exact smoothing settings and position-specific thresholds are outside its scope.

Uses Binance’s published index regimes for equity-linked perpetuals and its mark-based liquidation rules.

Sources indicate that indicates the documented pricing mechanism. Live prices, exact smoothing settings and position-specific thresholds are outside its scope.

The index feeds the mark, which Binance calculates separately from the latest executed trade.

If an adverse move leaves too little collateral to keep the position open, Binance can forcibly close it while the ETF market is shut. Under Binance’s liquidation rules, the mark triggers that process when it reaches the position’s liquidation threshold.

Binance normally limits the weekend and holiday gap between the mark and the index to 3% in either direction for equity-linked perpetuals and can adjust the limit in extreme conditions.

A trader can be right about where IBIT shares will reopen and still be forced out of the perpetual over the weekend if Binance’s mark crosses the liquidation level first.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Invesco confirmed a government money market fund on Nov. 17 that gives eligible institutions a way to hold part of their stablecoin reserves in fund shares recorded on Ethereum.

If a stablecoin issuer needs dollars from the fund to pay customers, it has to redeem those shares on the fund’s business-day schedule.

It has been revealed that the Invesco Stablecoin Reserves Onchain Fund (IROXX) is initially aimed at institutions such as stablecoin issuers and digital asset infrastructure providers. Its shares represent an investment in short-duration US Treasury securities and other eligible reserve assets. Holding a stablecoin alone gives a customer no right to redeem shares in the fund.

Investors in supported jurisdictions need an approved Superstate account and a verified wallet on the allowlist to hold IROXX on the Ethereum network.

The standard initial minimum is $1 million per fund account, and Invesco or an intermediary can combine master accounts and subaccounts to meet it.

To redeem, shareholders submit a request through the Investor Portal run by Superstate, the fund’s sub-transfer agent.

Under the fund’s redemption terms, Superstate normally sends a dollar wire on the next business day if it receives a valid request before 5 p.m. Eastern. For a request received after the cutoff on a business day, the fund normally prices the redemption and sends the wire on the next business day.

Sources indicate that the price is the next net asset value per share calculated after Superstate receives the request in good order. The ordinary payment terms allow up to seven days after Superstate receives a request in good order.

Early closes can affect same-day payment, and the fund can also withhold same-day payment in the 30 minutes before it calculates the share price.

A fund business day depends on the New York Fed, the fund’s custodian, and its main portfolio markets being open. Management also has to judge that the market can handle purchase and redemption requests.

Shareholders pay blockchain transaction fees, known as gas, on redemptions. Congestion or insufficient gas can delay a request past the cutoff even if the shareholder starts the transaction before it.

According to recent reports, investors can also elect USDC proceeds through a third-party intermediary, with the service setting its own onboarding and conversion terms, including when it delivers the tokens. The fund’s normal wire schedule gives investors a timetable for when dollars are sent, while USDC delivery depends on the intermediary.

Superstate’s normal dollar wire schedule for valid redemption requests on a fund business day.

The wire schedule tells investors when the fund sends the money.

The prospectus allows up to seven days under ordinary payment terms. The fund may also decline same-day payment shortly before it calculates the share price.

Recent findings suggest that compare valid Investor Portal requests received on the same fund business day. The two branches show the normal dollar wire schedule specified in the prospectus. The USDC strip identifies the separate conversion service.

The prospectus allows up to seven days under ordinary payment terms. The fund may also decline same-day payment shortly before it calculates the share price.

Industry News: Binance Claims It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (646 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, binance states it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday.
  • In a recent development, reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator.
  • “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, binance states it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers.

In a recent development, reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to.

“We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss remarked.

Recent findings suggest that binance has noted about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report. That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it states was affected.

It has been revealed that most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether remarked it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts.

The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice states government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva remarked the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action.

It has been revealed that binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the firm stated.

Industry observers note that from there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance.

It has been revealed that the FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has stated the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster.

That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it.

According to recent reports, binance has already said it replaced the affected assets with manufacturer funds, using part of its SAFU emergency fund and its corporate treasury. Withdrawals resumed in phases earlier this month, and the exchange aims to reopen all remaining networks and assets by the end of this week, Reuters reported.

In a recent development, on Wednesday, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters at the Singapore FinTech Festival that the firm plans to expand into five Asian markets in 2027 and does not need to raise new funds. He said talks are under way with five or six markets, three of them at a mature stage, and details are due in the first quarter.

Seker noted the cost of replacing the stolen tokens was “statistically” not a large amount for the firm. “In terms of the impact to us, we can take the impact and we can weather it without any change to the way we operate,” he said.

‘Dune: Part Three’: An Exclusive First Look at the Sets

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, nothing about the cinematic language of Dune is small—director Denis Villeneuve’s film trilogy does span multiple planets, after all.
  • Recent findings suggest that “My approach has always been with symbolism and semiotics,” Vermette tells AD.
  • Sources indicate that in conversation with Vermette about the sci-fi epic, examples of that core tenet come up often.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, nothing about the cinematic language of Dune is small—director Denis Villeneuve’s film trilogy does span multiple planets, after all. But throughout his work on the movies, including the upcoming Dune: Part Three, production designer Patrice Vermette has made sure to stay focused on the little details.

Recent findings suggest that “My approach has always been with symbolism and semiotics,” Vermette tells AD. “It is my philosophy of design, because for Denis, empty design cannot exist. Things need to have a purpose. Need to have a signification.”.

Sources indicate that in conversation with Vermette about the sci-fi epic, examples of that core tenet come up often. Carefully designed details imbue hidden meaning in each set, creating a captivating, immersive on-screen world that earned the designer an Oscar for his work in the first Dune. The trilogy’s latest installment, Dune: Part Three, which lands in theaters on December 18, expands on that ethos. And for the final film in the series, the sheer scale of the sets was larger. “It was our last chance working in that world,” Vermette states. “It’s like in a fireworks [display], it’s the end, it’s the bouquet final, it’s like, ‘alright, let’s do it!’”.

Robert Pattinson as Scytale, with director Denis Villeneuve.

Over 450,000 square feet of interior stages and 475,000 square feet of backlots were used for scenes shot in Budapest alone, with each set typically taking 14 to 16 weeks to build. (Filming also took place in Abu Dhabi and Iceland.) Even the sandworms that slither through the titular dunes got grander this time around: Instead of the relatively small platforms that were used to film worm-riding sequences as in the previous films, the production team built a 300-foot-long by 65-foot-wide sandworm in the middle of the desert.

Like in Dune: Part Two, Vermette was challenged to create entirely fresh sets for this installment, which adapts Frank Herbert’s 1969 novel Dune Messiah. One of the new settings viewers can expect is Wallach IX, the home of the powerful and secretive Bene Gesserit sisterhood. Throughout their planet, Vermette incorporated stone etchings that resemble human cells seen through a microscope, referencing the Bene Gesserit’s breeding program that has gone on for millennia. Mother nature also informed the architecture. “When you arrive on the planet, the buildings are basically eggs of a spider, like crops of spider eggs as you find them in nature,” Vermette explains. “Ecology has always been a huge source of inspiration for me, and also for the storytelling it gives—you know, they’ve got their web across the universe, for the genealogy they create.”.

Another new setting is the Veteran’s District, where the Fremen, the native inhabitants of the desert planet Arrakis, retire after fighting in the catastrophic holy war spurred by Paul Atreides, aka Muad’Dib (Timothée Chalamet). In the previous films, the Fremen lived in communal residences lined with hand-carved stone that recorded their history and culture. Returning from the battlefield, they find mass-produced housing units instead of the “green paradise” they were promised would await them. Made of ceramic instead of rock, with stamped-on rather than hand-carved markings, the Veteran’s District represents an artificial facsimile of their former homes. “And when you put all these units together, and you look at the rooftops, it’s there to represent sand dunes,” Vermette explains. “All these triangles align [to look like dunes], but it’s fake.”.

Another circular doorway represents an all-seeing eye near the lush Imperial Gardens, which illustrate Paul’s extreme wealth and control of resources—including water—on the dry planet of Arrakis.

In a recent development, there is a green paradise on Arrakis, just not for the Fremen. Lush gardens grace the planet’s Imperial Palace, a massive inverted pyramid with a large circle cut out of it—a reimagined version of the all-seeing eye. “I got inspired by the title of the book, Messiah, and from the fact that Denis, just like Frank Herbert, wanted to make sure that Paul Atreides was not going to be seen as a hero, and it’s a tale of being cautious about messianic figures,” claims Vermette. Similar representations of the all-seeing eye are found throughout the palace, sinisterly implying that Muad’Dib is always watching.

In actuality, Muad’Dib’s personal quarters are completely isolated from the rest of the palace. His wife, Irulan (Florence Pugh), must find her way through a twisting mass of hallways to reach him. “Basically, she’s walking into the psyche of Paul,” Vermette explains. “She goes into a void, and then it’s all these mazes of one’s mind.” When we get to the end of the maze, we see that Paul’s inner sanctum resembles a humble desert camp. Not unlike the Fremen, his dwelling has been reduced to an echo of what once was. He is “living as a recluse because he doesn’t trust anybody,” Vermette explains. “He wants to go back to a place where he felt the most comfortable, which was the desert. So he recreated that space.”.

“Denis really wanted that set to be the golden cage of Irulan,” Vermette says of these private chambers. “She’s married to the emperor, but she’s not free at all, she’s a prisoner.” The window is shaped similar to an infinity symbol, but is covered in metal screens. “It’s like eternity, but eternity is blocked. It’s like a cage.”.

In a recent development, the entrance to the maze within Muad’Dib’s inner sanctum. Vermette designed 40 maze wall panels that needed to be moved into various configurations to shoot the scene, which was filmed in less than a day. Eight people were each assigned a portion of the 12-foot-high panels and learned a choreography of sorts, swiftly moving into each configuration until they could do each one in five minutes or less. “We rehearsed and rehearsed, just like dancers or musicians; they knew exactly where to fit their pieces” within the roughly 14,400-square-foot space, states Vermette.

On the planet Wallach IX, the office of Bene Gesserit Reverend Mother Mohaim features stone carvings inspired by human cells under a microscope.

According to recent reports, the Imperial Palace throne room took 20 weeks to build. Behind Muad’Dib’s emerald throne, the windows are shielded with metal cast screens inspired by Montreal’s Saint-Ambrose Church, which was built in 1925 by architect Ernest Cormier.

The all-seeing eye is a repeating symbol Vermette inserted throughout the Imperial Palace, including a representation seen here as the circular entrance of Paul’s Keep.

The architecture of this Imperial Palace corridor has slanted walls to reflect a pyramid-shaped exterior and flying buttress support structures inspired by Gothic-style cathedrals.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • President Trump's official meme coin has reached latest lows since he suffered a major blow in the U.S.
  • Over the weekend, the TRUMP coin touched $0.896, marking the lowest point the token had ever stooped.
  • Industry observers note that luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt the midterms "added pressure to an already struggling token." Trading volume increased around the vote, and he believes some traders had bet on a Republican surprise win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Trump's official meme coin has reached latest lows since he suffered a major blow in the U.S. midterm elections. The token has dropped almost 40% since election day, and analysts warn that new congressional scrutiny could push it lower.

Over the weekend, the TRUMP coin touched $0.896, marking the lowest point the token had ever stooped. It has since bumped 8%, sitting at $0.965, which is still down almost 40% from election day and 98.7% from its all-time high of $73.43, set the day after it released, per Decrypt data.

Industry observers note that luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt the midterms "added pressure to an already struggling token." Trading volume increased around the vote, and he believes some traders had bet on a Republican surprise win. He mentioned there was a "visible unwind" that led to a "sharp drawdown" after the election results rolled out.

It has been revealed that "Democrats take both chambers in January and plan to use their subpoena power on his crypto ventures. His net approval rating has almost never been lower," Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt. "It is still possible this continues to decline and, therefore, has a negative effect on these Trump-affiliated assets.".

Other Trump-linked assets have also taken a hit. Since the election, World Liberty Financial's WLFI token has dropped 7.5%, per Decrypt data, and shares of the Trump Media & Technology Group have dropped 32%.

According to recent reports, trump launched TRUMP on January 17, 2025, three days before his second inauguration, which Shannon described as "close to the peak of his popularity." Since then, the coin has faced significant scrutiny over how much the President and his family have profited from it. (The First Lady following suit and launching her own meme coin didn't help matters.).

It has been revealed that the president’s crypto ventures also became a sticking point for the Clarity Act, a bill that aimed to provide a formal legal structure for most cryptocurrency activity. Democrats scrutinized the Trump family's involvement in the crypto industry, which profited them more than $1 billion in a year.

Recent findings suggest that A July draft would have barred public officials and employees, along with their spouses, from issuing or sponsoring digital assets while in office. That draft didn’t extend to officials’ children, including Don Jr. and Eric Trump, and the provision would have expired in January 2029.

It has been revealed that the bill failed a key Senate procedural vote in September. Patrick Witt, former executive director of the President’s Council of Advisers for Digital Assets, later said the “political issue of ethics really consumed everything else.”.

Recent findings suggest that TRUMP has "no value accrual, and it has been left in the dust of this narrative," Shannon said. "Google Trends indicates searches for $TRUMP essentially flatlining since June 2025.".

Recent findings suggest that nolan agreed, saying the coin’s appeal was "largely speculative," with no clear link between holding it and sharing in any underlying business success. The most it offered, he noted, was the exclusive dinner to the top holders, which was both popular and controversial, depending on who you asked.

"In my view, that was just an attempt to prop up the token without actually creating any long-term demand for it," he said.

In a recent development, interest in these dinners has dried up too. Ahead of the third gala scheduled for the event of the month, 185 holders of the token were invited to register, but only 130 wallets revealed on the final leaderboard. Those wallets held a combined $8.6 billion worth of TRUMP, according to Reuters, which is a 94% decline from the first dinner.

Recent findings suggest that then there's the "unappealing" token supply structure, Nolan said. The majority of tokens were allocated to Trump-linked entities and are being slowly unlocked, which means demand needs to keep growing to soak up newly injected supply.

"That is a difficult position for an asset whose main attraction is attention around one individual," he said.

Industry observers note that and what happens when Trump loses power? He has said he "would love" to serve a third term, but that remains unconstitutional—so the clock is ticking on his presidency.

"I think overall Trump leaving office probably means the token continues its gradual decline," Nolan told Decrypt. "Any big Trump headlines probably make it experience the same dead cat bounces (sharp rallies) we have seen it have during short periods of time.".

According to recent reports, shannon thinks Trump doesn't even need to lose power for the token to keep going down. He said that it is "incredibly unlikely" that the token reclaims its highs, as it would require it to boost 82x, too many investors have been burned, and the majority of the supply is still to be unlocked.

"I think the meme coin was doomed from the start, and like with most meme coins, creating long-term demand is a Sisyphean task," Nolan told Decrypt.

Recent findings suggest that aave Labs added Tron USDT deposits to the Aave App on Nov. 17 as it opened early access on Android.

TRON DAO remarked eligible users in supported jurisdictions can make the deposits on both Android and iOS. New Android users can download the app and join a waitlist, or use a Ghost Pass to start sooner, according to Aave Labs’ launch announcement.

Under Aave’s app disclosures, a user sends a supported stablecoin from an external wallet to the address the app provides. Funds that reach the user’s self-custodial account enter the pooled Stable Vault under the user’s signed instructions.

The vault checks the deposit asset’s price, issues shares, and records the position in a unit nominally worth one US dollar.

Industry observers note that the vault keeps its balance and withdrawal records on Arbitrum. Aave’s technical documentation identifies Ethereum mainnet as a chain where the vault can deploy funds to earn yield.

The pooled funds can move between approved strategies as deposits and withdrawals change the vault’s balances.

The withdrawal request burns vault shares and creates a dollar-denominated claim, which Aave calls an IOU. Under the vault’s redemption rules, users can convert principal into that claim.

Converting accrued interest requires the vault to have enough assets, above what it already owes, to cover the interest being claimed.

According to recent reports, settlement burns the IOU and pays out a supported token. The vault needs enough of that token on the payout chain, and a system-wide limit controls how much people can redeem over a given period.

Recent findings suggest that the redemption policy can also apply a fee that varies by asset. For example, a withdrawal in USDC depends on how much USDC is available on the redemption network, even if the saver originally funded the account with USDT.

According to recent reports, aave logs the vault position and withdrawal claim on Arbitrum. Redeeming that claim adds a separate liquidity check.

Sources indicate that A withdrawal request creates a claim. Settlement needs an eligible token and enough liquidity on the payout network.

It has been revealed that aave Labs indicates customers can request withdrawals at any time without a lockup. The app’s disclosures say market stress, a shortage of available liquidity or problems with a bridge can delay settlement or make it temporarily unavailable. The rollout gave no settlement timetable for Tron-funded withdrawals.

The Aave DAO earns a fee from the gap between what the vault earns and what it credits to savers, but third-party charges may also apply. Network or swap costs can arise separately if the withdrawal involves converting one stablecoin into another.

Tech Report: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine
