📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S.
  • In a recent development, tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S.
  • Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California remarked.

In a recent development, tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11.

Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together.

According to recent reports, from September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors noted. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information.

Sources indicate that the group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over.

The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims.

Industry observers note that the BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme.

In a recent development, police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC remarked. Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

Recent findings suggest that buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples.

Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed, that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since.

Recent findings suggest that reuters has described Scattered Spider as a loose-knit community of hackers suspected of breaking into dozens of U.S. companies. The DOJ release does not use the group’s name, but the BBC says Buchanan, a teenage hacker when the campaign began, was a member and a Justice Department spokesperson has previously tied the defendants to it.

The BBC stated Buchanan’s four co-defendants have all pleaded guilty and are serving time. It described the case as a years-long investigation involving authorities in the U.K., the U.S., Spain and Canada.

Sources indicate that scattered Spider has also faced prosecution in Britain. Two other members were jailed in the U.K. in July for a series of attacks, including one on Transport for London that caused £39 million in damage, the BBC said.

Industry observers note that the judge will set the amount of restitution at a hearing on Dec. 11, the final step in the case against the Scottish hacker.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As someone with frequent neck pain, I would give up my cozy sheets, white noise machine, and sunrise alarm clock if it meant I wouldn’t wake up with a stiff neck.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I think that a pillow can make a major difference in people that have a history of neck challenges," says Leia Rispoli, MD, an interventional pain management specialist and physiatrist at DISC Sport & Spine Center.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

As someone with frequent neck pain, I would give up my cozy sheets, white noise machine, and sunrise alarm clock if it meant I wouldn’t wake up with a stiff neck. (And that’s coming from someone who invests a lot in their sleep.).

Recent findings suggest that "I think that a pillow can make a major difference in people that have a history of neck challenges," says Leia Rispoli, MD, an interventional pain management specialist and physiatrist at DISC Sport & Spine Center. This is the very reason why I tend to lug my favorite pillow around on weekend trips.

There isn’t one pillow that works for everyone. Your best option depends on your sleep position, preferred firmness, body type, and whether you tend to overheat at night. To find the best pillows, our editors and testers slept on popular models from Purple, Casper, Coop, Saatva, and other leading sleep brands. We evaluated each one for comfort, support, temperature regulation, adjustability, ease of care, and value.

I love the Purple Harmony Pillow so much that I try to convert nearly everyone who mentions sleep within earshot of me. I even pack it for overnight trips. But it does feel unusual at first. Inside, a springy, ventilated latex core is wrapped in Purple’s GelFlex Grid, a flexible, honeycomb-shaped layer that bends under the weight of your head and springs back when you move. Together, these materials make the pillow feel buoyant rather than sink-in like memory foam.

Industry observers note that I tested the medium, 6.5-inch loft, meaning the pillow’s height before it is compressed. It provided enough height to support my head and neck while I slept on my side without feeling rigid. The materials give slightly beneath heavier areas, which helped reduce uncomfortable pressure around my head and neck. As someone who frequently experiences neck and back pain, I consistently felt comfortable and supported while sleeping on it.

Sources indicate that purple recommends the low, 5.5-inch version for most stomach and back sleepers. The medium and tall versions are generally better suited to side and combination sleepers, who often need more height to fill the space between the head and mattress. Body size and personal preference will also affect which height feels most comfortable.

The Harmony was also one of the coolest pillows I tested. Air circulates through the ventilated latex and open honeycomb layer instead of becoming trapped inside a solid block of foam. Its stretchy outer cover is also designed to draw sweat away from the skin so it can evaporate. Even on warmer nights, I rarely felt the need to flip the pillow over in search of a cooler surface.

Industry observers note that after nearly three years of regular use, my pillow has not developed noticeable lumps or gone flat. Its durable build helps justify the high price, but there are compromises. The pillow is unusually heavy, and some sleepers may notice the grid’s texture through the cover. Purple’s 30-night trial is also shorter than the trial periods offered by many competing brands.

In a recent development, still, no other pillow I tested delivered the same combination of responsive support, cooling, and long-term shape retention. I would purchase it again without hesitation.

Women’s Health art director Christine Giordano typically sleeps with two or three pillows, but the Casper Original gave her enough support to use fewer. “This pillow gave me the support I needed while still feeling light and airy,” she indicates. “It was breathable and didn’t clump, keeping me cool and comfortable at night.”.

It has been revealed that the Casper uses a pillow-within-a-pillow design: A firmer inner cushion provides structure, while a softer outer layer adds cushioning. Both layers are filled with polyester microfiber, a synthetic material made to feel light and fluffy like down. The construction prevented Giordano’s head from sinking too deeply while still giving the pillow a plush feel.

Giordano tries to sleep on her back but usually shifts onto her left side during the night. The pillow remained comfortable and supportive in both positions, making it a strong choice for combination sleepers who alternate between their backs and sides. However, stomach sleepers or people who prefer a flatter pillow may find its approximately nine-inch uncompressed height too lofty.

It has been revealed that the breathable cotton cover and airy synthetic fill also prevented the pillow from feeling stuffy during testing. It’s not as breathable as a dedicated cooling pillow, but Giordano did not notice heat buildup or need to flip it over for a cooler surface.

The entire pillow is machine-washable, which makes it easier to clean than models with foam or latex cores. Its soft filling may need occasional fluffing to maintain its shape, but Giordano did not notice clumping during testing.

In a recent development, at under $100, it is one of the more affordable pillows we tested. Giordano liked it enough that she replaced some of the other pillows in her home and purchased additional Casper ones for her family.

Women’s Health executive health and fitness director Jacqueline Andriakos, CPT, calls the Coop Original Adjustable the most comfortable pillow she has tried. “I’ve never been a pillow snob or had major complications with basic pillows from Amazon, but I noticed that this was far more comfortable than other, cheaper pillows I’ve used,” she states.

The pillow is filled with a blend of shredded memory foam and microfiber. Memory foam molds around the head and neck, while the soft synthetic fibers keep the pillow from feeling like a dense, solid block of foam. Unlike a pillow with a fixed height, the Coop can be unzipped so you can remove filling for a flatter feel or add more for extra support. The process can get messy, but that adjustability makes it easier to tailor the pillow to your body and sleep position.

Coop offers the pillow in classic, crescent, and cut-out shapes. Andriakos tested the classic and cut-out versions while switching between side and stomach sleeping. She preferred the cut-out, which has a curved indentation that creates room for the shoulder and allows the pillow to sit closer to the neck.

“I liked that it could wrap around my neck and shoulders, and I could almost cuddle it like a body pillow with an arm threaded underneath,” she says. Although the shape can look slightly awkward inside a standard pillowcase, it was super comfortable when she slept on her side.

It has been revealed that the pillow felt plush, but Andriakos’ head did not sink so deeply that her neck felt unsupported. She also found the outer cover breathable, although sleepers who regularly overheat may prefer a pillow specifically designed for cooling.

Because its height can be adjusted, the Coop can work for side, back, stomach, and combination sleepers. Side sleepers will generally need more filling to keep the head level with the spine, while stomach sleepers may prefer to remove enough filling to create a flatter surface. Finding the right amount may require a few nights of experimentation, but Coop’s 100-night trial gives you time to make those adjustments.

Recent findings suggest that it would take an exceptional pillow for me to consider replacing my Purple Harmony, but the Saatva Latex Pillow gave it serious competition. Although both pillows contain latex, they feel noticeably different. Purple uses one solid, springy latex core, while Saatva uses shredded pieces of latex surrounded by a soft layer of fine synthetic fibers. This gives the Saatva a plusher, more traditional feel, but it has enough structure to support the head and neck.

The pillow feels dense when you first pick it up, but my head settled gently into the soft outer layer without sinking too deeply. The shredded latex inside quickly returned to its original shape when I moved, so the pillow stayed supportive as I shifted positions. As a side sleeper who frequently experiences neck pain, I did not wake up with additional stiffness.

Saatva offers two heights. The standard version measures approximately four to five inches and is designed for back and stomach sleepers who generally need a lower pillow. The high-loft version measures approximately six to seven inches and is better suited to side and combination sleepers who need more height between their heads and mattresses.

I also appreciated that the pillow remained breathable throughout the night. The small spaces between the pieces of shredded latex allow air to circulate, while the cotton cover feels cool. It does not create the immediately cold sensation of a cooling pillow, but I did not notice uncomfortable heat buildup.

The outer layer is filled with microdenier fibers, which are very fine synthetic strands designed to imitate the light, fluffy feel of down. You can machine-wash this outer layer and its cotton cover, but the inner latex core must be removed and kept out of the washing machine.

According to recent reports, at $165 for a standard/queen size, this is one of the more expensive pillows we tested. Saatva also provides only 45 days for returns, which is shorter than the trial periods offered by several competitors. Still, its combination of plush cushioning, responsive support, and breathable materials makes it an excellent choice for sleepers who want a luxury-hotel feel that’s still supportive.

Industry observers note that for hot sleepers, a breathable pillow can be the difference between a good night’s sleep and a night spent tossing and turning. The Slumber Cloud UltraCool stood out because its cooling effect was immediately noticeable during testing.

It has been revealed that women’s Health managing editor Laura McLaughlin described the sensation as “a little sci-fi” because the surface felt immediately cool when she rested her head on it. The cover contains Outlast, a material designed to absorb excess body heat when you become warm and release it as your skin cools. This helps prevent heat from collecting around your head and face, although the effect may be less noticeable beneath a thick pillowcase.

McLaughlin also found the pillow easy to combine with others. “It’s great for layering with other pillows to get just the right height,” she says. “It’s neither too dense nor too high to use in combination with others already in place.” That makes it especially useful for sleepers who want additional height without placing a rigid pillow beneath their heads.

The interior is filled with polyester down alternative, a synthetic material designed to imitate the airy feel of down. It is available in soft/medium and medium/firm versions, allowing sleepers to choose how plush or structured they want the pillow to feel. The softer option will generally suit stomach sleepers or anyone who prefers more sink while the firmer version may provide better support for back and side sleepers.

The entire pillow can be machine-washed, a convenient advantage over pillows with foam or latex cores. However, synthetic filling can begin to clump after repeated use and washing, so it may require regular fluffing to redistribute the material.

Although the UltraCool does not provide the customized support of an adjustable pillow, it delivered the most noticeable cooling sensation of any model we tested.

According to recent reports, the Brooklinen Down Alternative Pillow is built for sleepers who want the fluffy feel of down without actual feathers. It’s filled with recycled poly microgel, a cluster of fine synthetic fibers that creates a light cushioning similar to down.

Unlike many pillows that come in only one firmness, this one is available in soft, medium, and firm versions. Brooklinen recommends the soft pillow for stomach sleepers who generally need less height beneath the head; the medium for back sleepers; and the firm for side sleepers who typically need more support to fill the space between the head and mattress.

It has been revealed that its cotton sateen shell feels smooth and has a subtle sheen. The pillow is also certified by OEKO-TEX Standard 100, which means its materials have been tested for a list of regulated substances. That certification does not evaluate the pillow’s comfort, durability, or environmental impact.

Brooklinen allows most products to be returned within 365 days, although it deducts a $9.95 return fee from the refund. That’s one of the most generous return windows we’ve seen.

In a recent development, the pillow can be machine-washed in cold water and tumble-dried on low with wool dryer balls until completely dry. As with most pillows filled with loose synthetic fibers, it may require regular fluffing to redistribute the fill and preserve its shape.

According to recent reports, A pillow’s height, or loft, should keep your head and neck aligned with your spine. Side sleepers generally need a taller pillow, back sleepers a medium-height pillow, and stomach sleepers a low pillow. Your mattress matters, too: The more deeply your shoulders sink into it, the less pillow height you may need. Most of the pillows we tested fell in the five- to nine-inch range, offering different levels of support depending on their material and sleeping position.

Side sleepers often benefit from a medium-firm or firm pillow that maintains its height. Back sleepers generally need medium support while stomach sleepers may prefer something softer that compresses easily. Because firmness labels vary by brand, consider the pillow’s material and height as well.

In a recent development, “There isn't one brand that's the magical brand for everyone,” indicates Rispoli. Look for a pillow that supports your head without tilting your neck sharply upward or downward. Adjustable pillows can help you fine-tune the height. Consult a health care professional if your pain is persistent, severe, or accompanied by numbness or weakness.

According to recent reports, memory foam molds around the head but may retain heat. Latex feels springy, breathable, and durable. Down is soft and airy but may lack structure while synthetic down alternative is usually easier to wash but may flatten over time. Hybrid pillows combine materials to balance cushioning and support.

It has been revealed that look for ventilated latex, shredded filling, or another construction that allows air to circulate. Some covers also absorb excess body heat or feel cool, although a thick pillowcase may reduce the effect. People who sleep cold may prefer denser foam or plush down filling that holds slightly more warmth.

As a sleep writer, I’ve tested all kinds of sleep accessories, from mattresses to eye masks, but pillows are probably my most-tested product category. (Unfortunately, I once tested so many pillows at the same time that I injured my neck, but I’ve learned my lesson.) To find the best pillows available online, I selected popular picks from leading sleep brands, like Purple, Casper, Saatva, Pluto, and more, for testing. Some helpful testers and I have slept on these pillows for dozens of nights to determine whether they’re worth the money, and our top pick has been my favorite pillow to sleep on for nearly three years. From flat pillow lovers to hot sleepers, our diverse crew of sleepers tried out eight pillows of various styles, materials, and price points.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The World Bank Group mentioned Nov. 17 that it would work with Citi and Circle to explore using USDC to settle development payments.

The group wants to see whether a dollar stablecoin can make those payments faster, cheaper, and more transparent.

Under the proposal, Citi would provide links to established banking networks, while Circle’s infrastructure would help problem USDC and settle payments in it.

The World Bank would examine where that route could work alongside its existing arrangements, which rely on correspondent banks to handle payments across banking networks.

Recent findings suggest that the initial exploration will engage borrower countries where digital assets are supported and permitted and focus on an intermediary-based model. The World Bank gave no launch date or list of participating borrowers, and said it would explore working with other banks over time.

The World Bank uses its original FundsChain platform to give project teams a record of where development money goes.

Sources indicate that authorized people can trace payments from the initial disbursement to the final recipient and inspect supporting documents. The group notes more than 350 projects across 96 countries are on the tracking platform.

Borrowers use the same process to apply for withdrawals, and projects continue paying suppliers and beneficiaries as before. FundsChain lets project teams document transactions through designated project accounts and local accounts farther down the payment chain.

The records can also feed into expenditure statements that borrowers submit through the bank’s client portal.

The World Bank wants to see whether stablecoin settlement could work alongside its existing banking arrangements.

The proposal leaves open exactly where USDC would enter the payment chain.

The World Bank gave no launch date, list of participating borrowers or measured cost or speed figures for the proposal.

The upper diagram follows the records FundsChain can capture. Dashed connectors show Citi’s and Circle’s proposed contributions to settlement. The payout note identifies an open design question.

The World Bank gave no launch date, list of participating borrowers or measured cost or speed figures for the proposal.

Industry observers note that linking an invoice to a transaction lets authorized reviewers check what a payment covered. That oversight can extend beyond the initial transfer to a borrower and into the spending that happens within a project.

The bank has separately explored whether it can build spending rules into payments themselves. In a July revision, it noted a FundsChain Evolution pilot had gone live in Ethiopia using programmable money to place conditions on how the funds can be spent.

The proposal leaves open where USDC would enter the payment chain, whether recipients would get tokens, and how any tokens would be converted to local currency.

Those details would determine what the change in settlement would mean for the people and organizations that ultimately receive the money.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s luxury brand, Denza, calls it “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles.” The new Denza N8 electric SUV will launch next week, offering an impressive CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles), massive digital screens, and plenty of premium extras.

After opening pre-orders for the new 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, stated the results so far “have been excellent.”.

According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.

That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

While Li confirmed last week that the upcoming EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.

Industry observers note that now, it’s official. Denza revealed on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.

BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.

The Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

It’s available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).

The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will use either a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) and 800 km (497 miles), respectively.

The Denza N8 also features BYD’s latest Flash Charging technology, letting it recharge from 10% to 80% in just five minutes. It takes just nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a fresh 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

Like most of its newly introduced luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.

Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.

The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.

BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

  • Six days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago, Nvidia delivered the best quarter in its history.
  • Fourth-quarter guidance came in at $130 billion against the $125.3 billion Wall Street wanted, with China assumed at zero.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

🖥️ Nvidia Beats, Board Says ‘No’ on Jensen.

Six days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago, Nvidia delivered the best quarter in its history. And told him he isn’t coming back.

Fourth-quarter guidance came in at $130 billion against the $125.3 billion Wall Street wanted, with China assumed at zero.

And the CFO raised their 2028 revenue outlook to 75% year-over-year growth.

Just an absolute smash all around.

Then board chair Harvey Jones got on the call and said it plainly. “The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” The directors unanimously accepted his resignation, and Jones declined to answer anything about the circumstances or the independent investigation still running.

Recent findings suggest that huang had publicly offered to come back hours earlier, saying he would do it if directors believed it served shareholders and employees. Trump and Elon Musk both backed the idea. A petition passed 182,000 signatures including nearly 9,000 self-identified Nvidia employees. None of it moved the room.

Sources indicate that nvidia has hired Heidrick & Struggles to run the permanent search. Colette Kress stays interim CEO while remaining CFO, with Jones saying the board has “every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity and ability to deliver.” The board also created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, to receive reports from the tech giant’s national security and trade compliance teams.

And after all of that—the stock rose about 3%.

A 6% revenue beat, guidance $5 billion above consensus, a new product cycle shipping, and the market gave it two percent. Shares sit roughly 35% below their October peak near $240. Nvidia perps on Hyperliquid were doing nearly a billion dollars of daily volume through the week, bouncing off $150 before settling near $162.

Recent findings suggest that as for impact on the broader AI trade, Nvidia proved AI demand is not collapsing. You cannot manufacture $107.6 billion of data center revenue, and margins at 74.8% mean nobody is discounting to move product. The demand-collapse thesis died on Tuesday.

Two details do belong to the bears though. Growth is decelerating from 103% to roughly 77% once you strip the extra week out of Q4 guidance. And gross margin guides down about three points, from 74.8% to between 71% and 72%. Slowing growth plus compressing margins is how multiples come down regardless of how big the absolute numbers get.

Recent findings suggest that the honest read is that the AI business is fine and the AI trade has stopped responding to it. For crypto that matters more than it should, because the correlation that dragged Bitcoin from $87,000 to the low $60s over six weeks ran through this exact trade.

Now we wait for the Fed on December 9 and insight into the 2027 rate hike cycle (or lack thereof) to determine the likely near-term fate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo aims to add across the US.

The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.

Industry observers note that the Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.

“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” remarked Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.

Sources indicate that EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

Sources indicate that smart move on EVGo's part. More reliable charger at a lower cost than they can build themselves, and Tesla takes on all the maintenance and network operations for a slice of the sales.

In a recent development, EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The company aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it plans to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

Before the sale, CoinShares held $43.2 million in treasury digital assets, including 235 Bitcoin worth $19.6 million, as of Sept. 30, according to its interim financial statements.

According to recent reports, the treasury also held $17.6 million in Ethereum and $5.9 million in Solana at that date. The October disclosure identified sales of Ethereum and Solana, with half the Solana position retained.

Recent findings suggest that the filing separately lists $4.1 billion of digital assets held for operations as of Sept. 30, including $880.5 million of Ethereum and $407.8 million of Solana. Some of those assets back exchange-traded products or hedge its obligations to product holders.

CoinShares declared the October sale before releasing its Q3 accounts on Nov. 18. The two disclosures show where shareholders still carry crypto risk.

The treasury sale reduced direct token holdings. Crypto prices still affect fees, and lending exposes the business to borrower defaults.

Stronger lending and trading lifted capital markets segment revenue and gains to $17.8 million from $4.9 million in the second quarter.

Industry observers note that whether or not she has the dreamy silverware to match, Sabre’s serving set with trendy burgundy handles will feel like a little luxury for plating cheese boards and opening bottles. The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in America outside of Tesla, but its larger three-row sibling looks like the better deal right now.

Through September, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 was the third top-selling EV in the US, behind the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.

Hyundai’s electric SUV is outselling rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, and Toyota bZ.

It has been revealed that why? For one, it’s one of the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at about $35,000, and Hyundai has been offering some of the most attractive lease deals.

After the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September last year, Hyundai responded by reducing prices on the IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims.

In a recent development, the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250. That’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model adds $2,500, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, starts at $58,955, or nearly $24,000 more than the base IONIQ 5 SE.

Recent findings suggest that on Hyundai’s website, the 2027 IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range is available to lease from $359 a month. The offer is for a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing for an effective cost of $567 per month.

The extended-range Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE RWD can be leased from $369 a month. The offer is also a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing, for an effective cost of $577 per month.

It has been revealed that hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9, meanwhile, is available to lease from $419 a month. That deal also includes $4,999 due at signing, but is for a 36-month lease, so the effective cost is $557 per month.

In a recent development, using Hyundai’s payment calculator, it would cost about $412 a month to lease the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE for 36 months with $4,999 due at signing. With an effective cost of $550 per month, it’s only $7 less than the three-row IONIQ 9.

The Hyundai IONIQ 9 offers more range than its smaller sibling, with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles for the base SE trim.

According to recent reports, the IONIQ 5 is a midsize electric SUV, about the same size as a Tesla Model Y, with two rows and enough room for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating and six- or seven-seat configurations.

With an added row of seating, the IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with the IONIQ 5, which offers up to 106.5 cubic feet.

While the IONIQ 9 may be the better deal right now, the IONIQ 5 is still a good fit for those looking for a smaller, more efficient SUV that doesn’t necessarily need the added space.

It has been revealed that in comparison, the standard Tesla Model Y RWD is listed for lease starting at $499 a month with an EPA range of up to 321 miles. That’s for a 36-month lease with $3,000 down.

Using Tesla’s payment calculator, if you put the same $4,999 down for a 24-month lease like the IONIQ 5, the Model Y RWD’s monthly rate is $549.

In a recent development, which one would you choose? The IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, or Tesla Model Y? Let us know why in the comments.

Both the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are built at Hyundai’s Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

It has been revealed that I really haven’t seen much value in leasing. I’d rather buy the car outright using cash, with the goal of keeping the car for 10+ years.

According to recent reports, my family recently bought a Hyundai IONIQ 5, and it is an outstanding car. Loaded with great features — both on the EV side and then for safety and comfort.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told us that its electric SUVs are attracting fresh buyers to the brand at a higher rate than its gas or hybrid vehicles.

The IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin, gold, and silver had already fallen on Wednesday before the Federal Reserve released its October meeting minutes.
  • Almost all participants at the October meeting judged that further rate increases would likely be appropriate in the months ahead under their baseline outlooks for inflation and employment.
  • It has been revealed that bitcoin traded in the $62,000 zone for most of the day after the minutes, while spot gold closed down 3% to $3,741.82 an ounce, and silver fell 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin, gold, and silver had already fallen on Wednesday before the Federal Reserve released its October meeting minutes.

Almost all participants at the October meeting judged that further rate increases would likely be appropriate in the months ahead under their baseline outlooks for inflation and employment.

It has been revealed that bitcoin traded in the $62,000 zone for most of the day after the minutes, while spot gold closed down 3% to $3,741.82 an ounce, and silver fell 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce. Gold had touched its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session.

Even after the minutes, CME FedWatch odds were 92% for a quarter-point hike in December and 8% for a half-point move.

Analysts linked the drop in bullion to the stronger dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of tighter policy. Gold pays no interest, so rising yields increase the cost of holding it instead of putting cash into interest-bearing assets.

The Silver Institute’s 2026 market forecast projects a 3% decline in overall industrial use, even as demand outside photovoltaics is expected to grow 4.5%. The institute still expects total silver demand to exceed supply by 35 million ounces this year.

The October minutes show a committee that held its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% by a 10-2 vote.

Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase, while a couple of participants noted a move larger than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if inflation data were unfavorable.

Sources indicate that bitget analyst Lewis Huang shared in a note that the record points to wider backing for a hike than the vote count shows. He stated:.

Industry observers note that “The minutes suggest broader support for an October hike than the 10–2 vote alone implied—and that was before payrolls and CPI both came in hot. Governor Waller has mentioned a half-point increase should be considered; evidence that other officials were already open to that scale of tightening in October could push the odds of a 50-basis-point move higher.”.

Sources indicate that huang pointed to yields and the dollar as the channel into Bitcoin, saying that a further rise in yields and the dollar would add pressure to Bitcoin, which is now trading well below its 200-week moving average near $68,000. Gold could also struggle if real yields keep climbing.

Industry observers note that fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank, sees the same path. He said:.

“Markets already price a run of hikes into next year, and the minutes suggest the committee was leaning that way even before October’s hot CPI.”.

Dori added that this likely keeps long-term yields and the dollar firm, and the question for Bitcoin is whether debasement concerns and advancing institutional adoption can outweigh it.

Fed staff also outlined that falling prices could force investors to sell assets to cut borrowing, while withdrawals could force fund managers to raise cash.

In very severe scenarios, sales by hedge funds, bond mutual funds and target-date funds could be large enough to impair market functioning. Staff were concerned that selling into a falling market could push prices down further and strain trading.

Fed staff outlined a scenario in which falling prices could force investors to cut leverage and fund managers to meet withdrawals.

Sources indicate that both routes can lead to asset sales. If selling deepens the fall, it can increase the pressure to sell again.

The diagram illustrates a hypothetical stress scenario discussed in October. Line lengths and widths do not encode size or likelihood.

It has been revealed that qualitative schematic of the October 27–28 Federal Open Market Committee minutes’ financial stability discussion. Dashed arrow reveals a possible feedback effect.

Industry observers note that the diagram illustrates a hypothetical stress scenario discussed in October. Line lengths and widths do not encode size or likelihood.

A softer dollar and lower Treasury yields would ease some pressure on markets, and Bitcoin’s own demand gauges give investors another way to judge a rebound.

Recent findings suggest that farside Investors’ ETF flow table demonstrates over $310 million in net outflows from US spot Bitcoin funds on Nov. 17 and 18.

It has been revealed that glassnode’s Nov. 17 analysis estimated that about 20% of the coins held by short-term holders were acquired between $62,000 and $66,000. That puts Wednesday’s reported price near the low end of a range where many recent buyers entered.

According to recent reports, using the same Nov. 17 data, Glassnode modeled a cluster of potential long liquidations between $59,500 and $62,200, where a renewed decline could force some leveraged positions to close.

Glassnode puts short-term holders’ overall cost basis at $74,100, and a return to that level would bring recent buyers back around break-even as a group.

Huang named the weekend low as the level to watch:.

“For Bitcoin, a break below the weekend low near $62,000 could extend the sell-off,” he said.

Stablecoin supply had shrunk 4.2% over 90 days, and Bitcoin briefly traded at a premium on Coinbase around the November low before slipping back to a small discount relative to the global price.

Georges Chouchani, founder and CEO of Euclid, links the minutes to that cash shortage:.

“The minutes show support for a hike went well beyond the two officials who voted for one in October, so markets start pricing more hikes after December.”.

In a recent development, he stated that this keeps yields and the dollar firm, and it hits a crypto market already short of cash. Stablecoin supply, the dollar tokens crypto trades with, has fallen by about $16 billion over the past month, its steepest drop since June 2022, so there are fewer buyers to absorb the selling, and Bitcoin takes the hit.

A premium that holds, sustained ETF inflows, or a leveling off in stablecoin supply would give investors more evidence that demand is returning.

Apollo’s newest electric scooter is also its lowest-cost yet

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market.
  • The upcoming Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the manufacturer’s Black Friday sale running through November 30.
  • The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the tech giant is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.

The upcoming Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the manufacturer’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo states the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.

The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.

Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.

At 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an important compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.

Recent findings suggest that despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.

Apollo claims it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance issues. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.

According to recent reports, perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The company indicates 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.

At $599, the Dash appears designed to get those riders into Apollo’s ecosystem much earlier – while also putting the firm squarely into competition with the mass-market scooters it previously sat above.

And for those wanting a bit more power or features, Apollo’s more upmarket models are on sale now as part of early Black Friday promotions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the New York Stock Exchange’s owner, is working with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.
  • The proposed venue would have to attract its own buy and sell orders, Hyunsu Jung, CEO of Nasdaq-listed Hyperion DeFi, told CryptoSlate.
  • Jung said firms quoting on both the proposed US venue and existing overseas markets could help keep prices close if the venues match orders and handle funding similarly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the New York Stock Exchange’s owner, is working with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.

The proposed venue would have to attract its own buy and sell orders, Hyunsu Jung, CEO of Nasdaq-listed Hyperion DeFi, told CryptoSlate.

Jung said firms quoting on both the proposed US venue and existing overseas markets could help keep prices close if the venues match orders and handle funding similarly.

The amount a trader can buy or sell at those prices would depend on the orders available on the US market. Jung’s firm builds on Hyperliquid and earns revenue from work in its ecosystem.

ICE announced the agreement on Oct. 29 and mentioned it would be the exclusive operator of the regulated markets, using a dedicated retail venue and clearing structure separate from its institutional futures business.

ICE also declared a minority investment in Trade[XYZ], subject to regulatory approvals, including approvals needed to support leveraged trading. ICE’s announcement sets out who would operate and clear the market, leaving the trading rules and exact order-book design unspecified.

Recent findings suggest that perpetual futures let traders take positions on the price of a reference asset through a contract with no set expiration date. Trade[XYZ] already offers contracts on equities, stock indexes, commodities and currencies to eligible customers outside the US.

ICE expects customers who pass identity checks to access the proposed market through participating futures brokers, formally known as futures commission merchants, and also expects its joint venture with OKX to help distribute the contracts.

That route depends on separate approvals for the venture’s broker-dealer and futures commission merchant businesses.

The existing HIP-3 design gives each builder-deployed venue its own order books and margining on Hyperliquid’s shared trading infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that in its November quarterly filing, Hyperion DeFi described ICE and Trade[XYZ]’s strategy in the context of HIP-3, an optional extension that lets operators control access. The filing tied the prepares it discussed to regulatory approvals, finalizing the extension, and making it available on the live network.

In a recent development, an order book records what buyers and sellers are willing to trade at each price, so a buy order posted outside the US would be available to traders on that book. To complete a trade on a separate US venue, a customer would need a matching order on the US book.

It has been revealed that hyperliquid’s existing builder markets keep separate order books. ICE has proposed a US route for verified retail customers.

A separate US order book would need its own buy and sell orders.

ICE’s final order-book design remains unspecified. The proposed access route depends on regulatory approvals. The drawn orders are illustrative.

In a recent development, A schematic of Hyperliquid’s documented HIP-3 architecture alongside ICE’s proposed customer access route. The solid line indicates existing architecture, while dashed lines indicate the proposed US setup.

ICE’s final order-book design remains unspecified. The proposed access route depends on regulatory approvals. The drawn orders are illustrative.

If a comparable contract traded at a higher price on one venue, a firm able to trade both could buy on the cheaper venue and sell on the more expensive one. Those trades would tend to bring the two prices closer.

A market maker that takes the other side of a customer’s trade in the US could manage some of the resulting exposure overseas if it can access both venues.

In a recent development, jung said margin and leverage rules for futures broker accounts would help determine how much liquidity firms can provide. Margin is the collateral a firm sets aside to support a position, and the more collateral a trade requires, the more of a firm’s capital it ties up.

Trade[XYZ] recorded over $4.9 billion of the $5 billion traded across tracked HIP-3 venues in the 24 hours through Nov. 18, representing 97.6% of the total. EntropyIO, the next-largest venue by volume, accounted for 2.3%, according to UnderHyper’s venue breakdown.

UnderHyper’s measure of rolling dollar volume counts completed trades across the HIP-3 venues it tracks.

Jung attributed Trade[XYZ]’s lead to listing key markets early and making them available in the Hyperliquid interface traders already used.

ICE hopes to reach US customers through brokers and distribution partners, but the size of that customer base and how often it trades will become clear only if the US venue opens.

If the US venue opens, traders will be able to judge its liquidity by the gap between the best buy and sell prices and how much they can trade near those prices. The test for ICE will come when traders try to move a large position near the price they first saw.

Amazon set to deploy more than 3,000 TATA electric delivery trucks

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, amazon isn’t just electrifying its American delivery operations.
  • Industry observers note that indian automaker TATA Motors has announced a deal with Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India.
  • In a recent development, “India is accelerating towards electric mobility and the realization of Viksit Bharat 2047,” notes Shri H.D.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, amazon isn’t just electrifying its American delivery operations. The virtual major box stores that Bezos built understands the benefits of EVs as well as anyone, and they’re working hard to deploy electric vehicles everywhere they can. And now, that global push is extending to India.

Industry observers note that indian automaker TATA Motors has announced a deal with Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India. When it goes live, it will be the largest electric truck deployment by in India and mark Amazon’s most significant move to extend its Indian fleet electrification beyond last-mile logistics.

In a recent development, “India is accelerating towards electric mobility and the realization of Viksit Bharat 2047,” notes Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy, Hon’ble Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Government of India. “The collaboration between TATA Motors and Amazon demonstrates what that looks like in practice: sustained demand from a nationwide logistics network met by electric trucks manufactured in India. Through PM E-DRIVE, the Government will continue to support this transition, and I look forward to more such efforts in powering green logistics.”.

In addition to being a significant deal for TATA, the 3,000 electric truck deal represents a serous bump to India’s deployed electric truck fleet, and are a major step towards the wide-scale electrification of freight transportation across the country – that’s not just good for Amazon’s fuel bills, it’s good for everyone and everything that breathes air, too.

“Electrifying our logistics and transportation network is an notable part of Amazon’s goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040,” states Abhinav Singh, Vice President, Operations, Amazon, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkey. “We have made significant progress in India, with more than 15,000 electric vehicles operating across 500-plus cities. To enable this transition, we are also supporting the development of infrastructure and solutions that make EV adoption easier for our carrier partners and drivers. We are now setting a bold vision to scale electric trucking, addressing one of the toughest challenges in decarbonizing transportation. Our collaboration with TATA Motors marks an important step towards realizing this vision. By combining our strengths, we aim to accelerate the deployment of electric trucks across more routes, starting with intracity operations and expanding to India’s major freight corridors.”.

Sources indicate that the truck Amazon will be deploying in these record numbers is a version of the Tata Ultra E.7, a 7.5-tonne (~16,000 lb.) straight truck powered by a 240 kW (~320 hp) electric motor drawing power from a 96 kWh LFP battery pack. The truck’s makers claim a loaded range of up to 130 km (~80 miles) on a single charge, with DC fast-charging that’s capable enough to keep the trucks charged up between deliveries.

Amazon’s newly introduced TATA electric delivery trucks will support the transport of goods between warehouse facilities – which means traveling across cities and along India’s national freight corridors.

In a recent development, with Thanksgiving just around the corner, I’ve already started thinking about two very notable things: what’s going on the dinner table and what I’ll wear. I’m especially looking forward to my mom’s baked mashed potatoes (a family favorite) and the homemade mac and cheese I’ll be bringing along. But, especially as a style writer, half the fun of the holidays is having a good excuse to put together a good outfit.

In a recent development, my family’s Thanksgiving gatherings tend to be pretty casual, so I’m not one to show up in anything overly dressy or uncomfortable. I’m usually somewhere in the middle, opting for an outfit that looks like I made an effort but still lets me enjoy a second helping of stuffing without worrying about a too-tight waistband. Think a great sweater with loose-fitting jeans, a knit dress with boots, or even a smartly-styled leggings outfit. Because as much as I love dressing up for the holidays, I also want to enjoy post-dinner card games or sit comfortably on the couch afterward.

Industry observers note that if you’re approaching Thanksgiving dressing the same way, I’ve rounded up six outfit ideas to help get you inspired. I’ve included a few options perfect for a Christmas card photoshoot, along with more laid-back looks that are just as fitting for a casual family gathering. No matter what your holiday intends look like, these outfits strike that happy medium between looking good and feeling comfortable. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have some mac and cheese to make.

In a recent development, in my opinion, there’s no outfit more perfect for the holidays than a sweater dress and boots. It’s cute enough for family photos but loose and soft enough to keep you comfy all day (especially if you kick the boots off at the door). Grab a long-sleeve knit dress that hits somewhere between mid-thigh and the knee and pair it with some fleece-lined tights and your fave knee-high boot. A midi or maxi dress with an ankle bootie works too.

Express Mock Neck Mini Sweater Dress.

Sam Edelman Sylvia Knee-High Boot.

Start by pulling out a denim jacket and denim skirt. From there, add a plain white T-shirt. I love brown for the fall, so I wore my version of this outfit with brown boots and a matching brown belt and bag. I love this combo because it looks super stylish, but I don’t feel overdressed or uncomfortable when I wear it. Don’t have a denim skirt or jacket? No problem. You can recreate this look with a leather jacket, jeans, or any neutral mini skirt.

Presics Supima Cotton Box Cut T-Shirt.

Sources indicate that start with a pair of satin or silk pants and pair them with a sweater and ballet flats in the same shade. This outfit has been one of my go-tos lately because it’s so comfortable, but the monochrome palette and shiny finish of the pants make it look like I tried way harder than I actually did. You can even make it feel a little dressier by swapping the flats for a pair of pointed-toe ankle boots.

Sources indicate that it doesn’t get comfier than leggings and slippers. For ultra-casual gatherings when you just want to focus on family and food without looking frumpy, just style yours a little smarter. Go for a pair of leggings with minimal seaming (especially a pair without a front seam), which makes them look sleeker. Then grab a dressy-looking oversized sweater—something with a boxy cut, a turtleneck, or a nice knit. I find that my tweed stitch J. Crew Rollneck Sweater is perfect for this look. Finish it off with a neutral slipper and a pair of scrunchy socks.

Crz Yoga SculptAir No Front Seam Leggings.

According to recent reports, opt for a pair of baggier jeans for this more casual outfit, which will be way comfier than a restrictive skinny or straight-leg jean. A looser pant also pairs better with a cozy boot, like this platform ankle boot. Finally, throw on a long-sleeve top or sweater with a cute vest for an outfit that feels very fall.

Vaoyiu Faux Suede Shearling Lined Vest.

Banana Republic The Icon Classic Wide-Leg Jean.

Project Cloud Ankle Platform Boots.

Okay, you caught me—I actually wore this outfit for Christmas last year instead of Thanksgiving, but it definitely works for either holiday! For this combo, start with your favorite skirt and a turtleneck top. Then top it off with a relaxed-fitting blazer (I love this houndstooth blazer, but any pattern or solid color will do). On the bottom, throw on a pair of tights and a knee-high boot.

Arach&Cloz Sleeveless Turtleneck Sweater.

Honda just showed off its first high-end electric mountain bike

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes.
  • Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the upcoming Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market.
  • The RN0 was jointly developed with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes. Now the Japanese giant is adding another electrified vehicle to the list – a premium electric mountain bike.

Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the upcoming Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market. And unlike many automotive-branded e-bikes that amount to little more than a licensing deal and a familiar logo slapped on someone else’s frame, Honda appears to have actually put some engineering muscle behind this one.

The RN0 was jointly developed with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.

Industry observers note that there’s actually some real history behind that connection. Honda experimented with mountain bike development in the early 2000s, culminating in its wild RN01 downhill racing bike. In 2005, that project won the overall series championship in the UCI Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup. Honda never turned the RN01 into a consumer bicycle, but more than two decades later, the RN0 is effectively picking up where the firm previously left off.

Sources indicate that the roughly 24 kg (53 lb) RN0 is set up as a multi-role electric mountain bike, featuring 160 mm FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima front suspension paired with a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima rear shock. DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE wheels use a mullet setup with a 29-inch wheel up front and 27.5-inch wheel in the rear, while Shimano DEORE XT four-piston brakes handle stopping duties.

Those are some quality components, but the drivetrain may be even more interesting.

Honda is using Shimano’s new 2.3 kg drive unit, rated for up to 100 Nm of torque and 750 watts of maximum output, paired with a sizeable 720 Wh battery.

Shimano’s AUTO ASSIST can automatically vary motor assistance based on terrain and rider input, while AUTO SHIFT handles gear changes to maintain an appropriate cadence.

There’s even an Assist Carryover function that briefly continues providing power after pedaling stops, potentially making it easier to clear rocks, roots, and other technical obstacles that normally would see the assist grind to a halt right when it is needed most.

A 2.2-inch color display is integrated directly into the top tube, and there’s USB-C charging plus Shimano app connectivity for adjusting motor settings and electronically locking the bike.

Honda hasn’t yet declared pricing in its release, but with a carbon chassis, Factory-level FOX suspension, XT brakes, and premium Shimano electronics, don’t expect this to be the everyman’s electric bike.

If anything, the RN0 looks much more like Honda is finally bringing its motorcycle engineering mentality back to mountain bikes – this time with a battery and motor along for the ride.

Bitcoin flashes a signal seen at four previous market bottoms as $62,000 comes under pressure

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Bitcoin rebound from just above $62,000 was weaker the second time.
  • 18 lows were $62,006 and $62,063 on the daily candles.
  • 19 analysis for CryptoQuant, Woominkyu put 30-day net realized losses at $8 billion, well short of two earlier 2026 readings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Bitcoin rebound from just above $62,000 was weaker the second time. The bounces came on Nov. 15 and 18, and the second session closed closer to its low. By then, a CryptoQuant measure showed the steepest losses since mid-August on older coins that moved. The next question is whether spot buyers can absorb that pressure for more than a day.

Sources indicate that the Nov. 15 and Nov. 18 lows were $62,006 and $62,063 on the daily candles. Bitcoin finished the first day at $65,351 and the second at $63,068.

It has been revealed that in a Nov. 19 analysis for CryptoQuant, Woominkyu put 30-day net realized losses at $8 billion, well short of two earlier 2026 readings. Glassnode’s Nov. 17 report found losses at levels it had seen around past market bottoms when measured against a year’s worth of realized profits.

Recent findings suggest that both gauges start from an estimate of what investors gained or lost when coins moved. Glassnode compares realized losses with profits taken over the previous year. On that relative measure, the weekend selloff reached readings Glassnode associated with lows in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023.

Recent findings suggest that glassnode’s ratio reached levels seen near past lows. CryptoQuant’s 30-day net loss was smaller than in February or June.

A steep wave of losses can stand out against past profits even when the 30-day net dollar loss is smaller than in earlier selloffs.

According to recent reports, the Glassnode article specifies the profit lookback. It leaves the exact loss window unstated. Both measures describe past coin movements.

The left branch demonstrates Glassnode’s ratio of realized losses to prior-year realized profits. The right branch shows CryptoQuant’s rolling 30-day net realized profit or loss. The branch layout is conceptual.

The Glassnode article specifies the profit lookback. It leaves the exact loss window unstated. Both measures describe past coin movements.

According to recent reports, cryptoQuant’s series tallies profits and subtracts losses over a rolling 30-day period. On that measure, net losses hit $30 billion on Feb. 20 and $18 billion on June 30. Even with a smaller monthly reading, losses were concentrated in the latest selloff. The four days from Nov. 15 to Nov. 18 produced $5 billion in net losses, more than half the 30-day figure.

A burst of losses can look extreme against a year’s profits while the month’s net dollar loss stays smaller than it was in a previous selloff. Earlier gains still in the 30-day window can offset part of the recent losses. Neither gauge sets a threshold Bitcoin has to reach before the price can stabilize.

According to recent reports, woominkyu’s Nov. 19 CryptoQuant Quicktake lists net losses of $30 billion on Feb. 20, $18.4 billion on June 30, and $8.4 billion in its latest reading.

Source: Woominkyu, CryptoQuant Quicktake.

That pressure reached coins that had been idle for more than 155 days. CryptoQuant’s long-term-holder spent output profit ratio fell to 0.73 on Nov. 18, its lowest since mid-August, according to Woominkyu’s analysis. The reading implies roughly 73 cents in value when those outputs moved for each dollar of value when they were created. The series measures only older outputs that moved, including transfers that can occur without a trade on an exchange.

In a recent development, the spot market gave a more tentative signal. Glassnode saw Bitcoin briefly trade at a premium on Coinbase around the Nov. 15 low before slipping back to a discount. Woominkyu put the Nov. 18 reading for CryptoQuant’s Coinbase Premium Index at minus 0.14%. That index compares the dollar price on Coinbase with the USDT price on Binance. It helps gauge relative buying pressure across venues using prices alone.

Glassnode also reported that buyer-initiated spot trades outweighed seller-initiated trades over the day leading into its Nov. 17 snapshot. Sustained buying in completed spot trades would give the rebound more weight. Standing buy orders can still be withdrawn.

The Upcoming York Fed calendar scheduled initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey for 8:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 19. Because the reports share a release time, a move in the two-year Treasury yield could reflect either or both. The yield was 4.80% on Nov. 18, unchanged from the day before in the Treasury’s daily series.

Industry observers note that bitcoin can respond promptly to a change in rate expectations. Daily on-chain readings take longer to fill in. If Bitcoin’s price stays above the recent lows, watch whether daily net losses ease and the older-coin ratio moves back toward 1, where spending and creation values are equal. A narrower Coinbase discount alongside sustained spot buying would add evidence that buyers can absorb the supply. A daily close near $62,000 while losses deepen and the discount persists would leave the rebound on weaker footing.
